The SHC should demonstrate an understanding of financial options to support specialty case acceptance, educating patients on treatment choices, overcoming common patient objections, and proactively keeping Specialists schedules productive for smooth specialty days. jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

Position Summary

The Patient Care Coordinator plays a key role in ensuring a positive and seamless experience for patients from their first point of contact through their treatment journey. This position combines customer service excellence, organizational skill, and administrative accuracy to manage scheduling, verify insurance, and support front office operations. The role requires professionalism, strong communication skills, and the ability to multitask in a fast-paced dental or medical practice environment.

Requirements

Scheduling & Coordination

Schedule, confirm, and manage patient appointments to ensure efficient provider schedules.
Coordinate follow-up appointments and rescheduling as needed.
Communicate clearly with patients about appointment requirements, preparation instructions, and timelines.

Patient Communication & Support

Serve as the first point of contact for patients, answering and directing high-volume calls in a professional manner.
Provide accurate information regarding office policies, treatment expectations, insurance coverage, and wait times.
Maintain a patient-focused approach, ensuring questions and concerns are addressed promptly.

Insurance & Financial Processes

Collect, review, and verify patient insurance information, including eligibility and plan benefits, before appointments.
Communicate potential out-of-pocket costs and obtain necessary authorizations when applicable.
Collaborate with billing or insurance coordinators to ensure claim accuracy.

Administrative Duties

Accurately perform data entry and maintain up-to-date patient records in the practice management system.
Ensure all necessary patient documentation is completed, scanned, and stored in compliance with HIPAA regulations.
Assist with general front office operations, including filing, faxing, and handling correspondence.

Collaboration & Workflow

Partner with clinical teams to coordinate patient flow and minimize wait times.
Assist team members during peak hours to ensure smooth operations.
Maintain a clean, organized, and welcoming front office environment.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

High school diploma or equivalent required; associate’s or bachelor’s degree preferred.
Minimum of 1 year experience in a dental, oral surgery, or medical office preferred.
Familiarity with dental/medical terminology and insurance verification processes.

Technical Skills

Proficiency with practice management software (WinOMS, Dentrix, Eaglesoft, or similar).
Competent in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook).
Strong data entry accuracy and attention to detail.

Soft Skills

Excellent communication and customer service skills.
Ability to multitask and prioritize in a high-paced environment.
Team-oriented mindset with problem-solving abilities.
Bilingual abilities are a plus.

401(k) with 3% Non-Elective Safeharbor Contribution
Health, dental, vision, and life insurance
Paid time off and sick leave
Flexible spending account
Uniform allowance
On-the-job training and career development opportunities

As a Patient Care Coordinator, you’ll be one of the first people our patients meet and an important part of their experience with us. You’ll bring our G3 approach—Greeting, Guiding and Gratitude—to life by creating meaningful connections with patients and making every visit feel personal, positive and easy.

Monday-Friday

Greeting: Create a warm, welcoming environment and make every patient feel valued from the moment they arrive.
Guiding: Support patients throughout their visit, including check-in/check-out, appointment scheduling, insurance verification and answering questions about their care.
Treatment Support: Help patients understand treatment recommendations, payment options and available financial arrangements.
Patient Experience: Build trusting relationships with patients and help make their dental experience comfortable and stress-free.
Communication: Answer phones, respond to patient questions and communicate clearly with patients, doctors and the dental team.
Scheduling: Maintain an efficient schedule and help maximize opportunities for patients to receive the care they need.
Gratitude: Show genuine appreciation for every patient and create an experience that makes them feel cared for and confident in choosing us.

Qualifications

1+ year of experience in a dental, healthcare, medical, hospitality or customer-service environment preferred.
Knowledge of dental terminology preferred.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
A genuine passion for helping people.
Ability to build rapport and create positive relationships with patients.
Strong organization and attention to detail.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.
A positive, professional and patient-first approach.

This isn’t just a front-office position. You’ll play an important role in helping patients feel comfortable, understand their care and take the next step toward a healthier smile.

You’ll have the opportunity to build relationships with patients, work alongside a supportive dental team and develop valuable skills in healthcare, customer experience and dental practice operations.

Previous experience in a dental or medical office setting

jobs.title: Program Coordinator II, Community Based Research Initiative (Community Engagement & Research Coordin
jobs.description:
Job Summary:

Under the general supervision of the Executive Director and Program Principal Investigator, the INSPIRE Programs Coordinator will manage the day-to-day operations of CDU’s growing portfolio of INSPIRE community-based research programs—INSPIRE Faith, INSPIRE CA, and INSPIRE USA. The Coordinator serves as the primary operational point of contact across these programs, combining research-program coordination, community relationship-building, and oversight of the digital engagement and data-capture platforms (in partnership with the technology team) that enable the programs to operate at scale. The role blends hands-on, place-based community partnership (primarily through INSPIRE Faith) with the coordination of predominantly online, largely automated statewide, and national programs. A central purpose of the role is to strengthen community trust in research and to broaden the participation of Black/African American/Hispanic communities and other communities of color in clinical research and trials, ensuring that community voice and priorities shape how the work is designed and carried out.
About the Center:
The Charles R. Drew University of Medicine and Science (CDU), a partner in the UCLA Clinical and Translational Science Institute (CTSI) alongside UCLA and Cedars-Sinai, is building a community-centered clinical research enterprise through its Clinical and Translational Research Center (CTRC) in South Los Angeles. The INSPIRE programs are a family of community-based research initiatives advancing health and brain health across diverse populations. INSPIRE Faith is a deep, place-based partnership with faith institutions requiring regular in-person engagement with community partners; INSPIRE CA, and INSPIRE USA are digitally delivered, largely automated programs conducted primarily online, with select live sessions led by physicians and study staff. Together they build on CDU’s longstanding legacy of community engagement and health-equity research.

This work advances a national commitment to health equity: expanding access to healthcare in underserved communities, building lasting trust between communities of color and the healthcare system, and increasing the participation of Black/African American communities and other communities of color in research and clinical trials. As a historically Black graduate institution, CDU pursues these goals in partnership with peer institutions and community organizations, treating community relationships not as a means of recruitment but as the foundation of research that is shaped by, accountable to, and beneficial for the communities it serves. The INSPIRE Programs Coordinator is central to this mission, serving as the trusted community bridge that connects faith and community partners to research and trial opportunities and helps ensure that the science reflects the priorities of the community.
Essential Duties

Manage the day-to-day operations and coordination of the INSPIRE research programs (Faith, CA, and USA), ensuring each program runs smoothly, on schedule, and in alignment with study protocols and the Center’s mission
Coordinate in-person activities for INSPIRE Faith—anticipated at approximately two days per week of on-site engagement with community partners—and support the logistics of live sessions conducted by physicians and study staff across all programs, including scheduling, participant coordination, and event execution.
Coordinate and support program staff, students, and volunteers across the INSPIRE programs, including onboarding, task coordination, and training
Support participant recruitment, retention, and outreach across programs, including coordinating culturally appropriate promotional and educational materials (in collaboration with the communications team)
Attend community meetings, faith-partner gatherings, health events, and program activities as needed to represent the INSPIRE programs and CDU
Oversee the online engagement platform, participant communications, scheduled calls, and data-capture elements for the digitally delivered programs (INSPIRE CA, and USA), coordinating closely with the technology team to ensure the platforms function reliably and participant data is captured accurately and securely.
Monitor program metrics, participant engagement, and feedback to assess effectiveness, support quality improvement, and inform recommendations to program leadership
Establish and support Faith Community Advisory Boards across Los Angeles, coordinating the formation of one board in 2026 and several additional boards by 2028. Each board is a governance body of no more than 11 faith leaders drawn from partnering faith institutions, guiding program direction, protocol input, and community voice at the faith-partner level. The Coordinator organizes board recruitment, scheduling, meeting logistics, and ongoing stewardship.

Recruit, onboard, and support Community Navigators from partnering faith institutions, growing the Navigator corps to 50 by the end of 2026 and more than 500 by the end of 2028. Navigators are community members who support the conduct of the studies from the faith-community side, including participant recruitment, guidance in navigating different community and clinical spaces, and support at program events. Navigators are distinct from advisory board members and are not study participants themselves.

Organize and help lead faith-based health festivals, coordinating planning, faith-partner engagement, logistics, staffing, and execution to advance community health and program visibility across partnering faith institutions.
Build trusted partnerships with community and faith-based organizations, serving as the primary liaison and fostering ongoing engagement across INSPIRE programs.
Advance community-centered research by connecting partners to clinical research opportunities, promoting diverse participation, and ensuring community voices inform program and study design through transparent and culturally responsive engagement.
Perform administrative tasks related to community engagement program management, such as creating reports, PowerPoint, and maintaining records
Support grant management and reporting for the programs—including tracking deliverables, timelines, and compliance, and coordinating with dedicated grant writers who lead proposal writing (this role is not responsible for writing grants)

Required Qualifications

EDUCATION:

Four-year college degree (B.A., B.S.) in Health Sciences. Experience in Business Administration, Public Administration, or Public Health is an advantage.

EXPERIENCE:

At least 2 or more years of experience coordinating research programs, studies, or educational/community programs, preferably in an academic, clinical research, or healthcare setting and activities.
Experience with grant or program management, including tracking deliverables, timelines, budgets, and reporting requirements for federal, local, or private funders (proposal writing is handled by dedicated grant writers and is not required for this role).
Experience in coordination of staff and students, including experience working in conjunction with HR. Also strongly prefer experience working with diverse partners and cultural sensitivity.
Demonstrated ability to build and sustain trusted relationships with community members, faith-based or community organizations, and diverse partners; experience with community-engaged or community-based work strongly preferred.
Understanding of, and commitment to, expanding access to healthcare and increasing the participation of Black/African American communities and other communities of color in clinical research and trials; familiarity with the trust barriers that affect research participation in underserved communities and with community-centered approaches to addressing them strongly preferred.
Experience recruiting, organizing, and supporting community advisory boards, community health workers or navigators, and community volunteers, ideally within faith-based settings; experience planning or leading community or faith-based health events or festivals strongly preferred.
Comfort with technology and digital tools; experience using online engagement platforms, virtual meeting/call coordination, databases, or electronic data-capture systems (e.g., REDCap) preferred. Ability to work closely with a technology team to support program platforms and data workflows.

Experience with developing and communicating, in written and oral form, detailed and technical scientific and administrative program information to various audiences.
Has experience developing evaluation metrics to assist Supervisor in reviewing effectiveness of program activities, recommending improvements, and assisting in executing recommendations.
Has experience developing marketing/promotional information to increase visibility of the institution or program. Prefer experience articulating detailed or technical scientific information in a generally publicly acceptable and culturally appropriate manner.
Ability to develop and maintain professional working relationships in complex program/organizational settings involving heterogeneous constituents such as academic and clinical faculty, staff, students, and community partners from diverse backgrounds.
Experience with interpreting operating policies and procedures and resolving minor discipline and other employee relations issues within an academic setting or institution.

SKILLS

Demonstrated experience developing and executing community engagement strategy
Proven ability to build relationships and partnerships with diverse groups
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Strong organizational and time-management skills
Budget development and oversight experience

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Prefer basic/working knowledge of Spanish language.
Proficient in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
Strong research-program coordination skills, including managing multiple concurrent programs, timelines, and deliverables with attention to protocol and compliance requirements
Comfort with online engagement platforms, virtual meeting tools, and electronic data-capture systems; able to partner effectively with a technology team

COMPLEXITY:

The ability to perform highly detailed work with sustained attention and care while providing/obtaining information on numerous inquiries is paramount to success in this position.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.  Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Long-term sitting at a computer workstation. Frequent standing and walking; occasional standing for multiple hours at events. Finger movement, feeling sufficient to work on computers and equipment; speaking clearly, hearing conversationally, and seeing far and near. Regular off-campus travel will be involved, including approximately two days per week of in-person engagement for INSPIRE Faith.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.  Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Occasionally required to work in confined space.
Occasionally required to work evenings or weekends to attend events or meet with community members.
May handle sensitive information

MENTAL DEMANDS:

The mental demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Able to perform highly detailed work with sustained attention

Behavioral Health Care Manager / Program Manager - Enhanced Care Management

Inland Empire, California

Akido builds AI-powered doctors .
Akido is the first AI-native care provider, combining cutting-edge technology with a nationwide medical network to address America’s physician shortage and make exceptional healthcare universal. Its AI empowers doctors to deliver faster, more accurate, and more compassionate care.

Serving 500K+ patients across California, Rhode Island, and New York, Akido offers primary and specialty care in 26 specialties—from serving unhoused communities in Los Angeles to ride-share drivers in New York.

Founded in 2015 (YC W15), Akido is expanding its risk-bearing care models and scaling ScopeAI, its breakthrough clinical AI platform. Read more about Akido’s $60M Series B. More info at Akidolabs.com.

The Opportunity

At Akido Care, we are redefining healthcare for underserved communities by addressing the needs of populations with complex medical and social challenges. As part of our ECM team in the Inland Empire, you'll be at the forefront of this mission, providing compassionate, impactful care.

We are hiring for two versions of this role, and this posting covers both. Which one fits depends on the experience you bring.

Behavioral Health Care Manager. You will serve as the team's behavioral health resource—contributing to care planning, providing direct patient support, and ensuring that patients in crisis or with unmet behavioral health needs are connected to the right level of care.
Behavioral Health Care Manager & Program Manager. In addition to serving as the team's behavioral health resource, you will supervise an interdisciplinary team of case managers, including but not limited to: a Registered Nurse, Care Coordinator, and Community Health Worker. This version carries a higher salary.

This is a hybrid role based in the Inland Empire, with regular in-person presence at Chaparral Medical clinics (particularly Pomona and Rancho Cucamonga clinics), community outreach in the field, and occasional travel to LA for all-hands meetings. Local candidates strongly preferred.

The minimum education requirement for both versions of this role is an MSW or MFT, with a California licensure (LCSW/LMFT) preferred. You will also need to reside locally to the region served.

What You'll Do — Behavioral Health Care Manager

Maintain a personal caseload of patients with behavioral health needs and deliver high quality care to patients.
Conduct behavioral health screenings and assessments to inform individualized care plans, developed in partnership with the patient and the interdisciplinary team.
Serve as the team's go-to resource for behavioral health questions, warm handoffs, and crisis response protocols—ensuring that patients presenting with suicidality, acute mental health concerns, or SUD crises are appropriately triaged and connected to care.
Document all encounters accurately and timely in Care Director in compliance with IEHP ECM program requirements, CalAIM standards, and HIPAA.
Serve as subject matter expert in team dependent topics such as harm reduction, and clinical case management.

User Research Assistant

We are looking for a detail-oriented User Research Assistant who has an intense passion for gaming and the science around conducting research. As a User Research Assistant, you will moderate groups (4 - 24 participants) through test sessions on console, PC, and mobile products where data is collected on our games. During this 7 - 18-month contract position you will observe participant behavior and communicate that information back to the research team. You will receive training for many of the necessary skills; however, knowledge of research practices with people is critical.

• Prepare and execute research studies.
o Support lead researchers in investigating gameplay behavior to uncover insights
o Support operational tasks including the setup of labs and procedures

o Contribute to high-quality research reports that synthesize qualitative and quantitative findings into clear, actionable insights for product, design, and engineering teams
o Support expert reviews (heuristic evaluations, UX audits, competitive assessments) to identify usability issues, experience gaps, and opportunities for improvement across game features, flows, or systems.
o Clean and code qualitative and quantitative data for analysis
o Use survey tools to draft, distribute, and administer surveys
o Use a database to search, filter, schedule, and communicate with playtest participants
o Recruit the necessary number and participant profile for each study
o Maintain the inventory of lab supplies, forecasting and updating when new stock is needed
o Special projects on occasion (Data entry, Recruiting events, Game teardowns, Documentation, etc.)

_ Qualifications

• Education:
o Completion of a relevant college degree (branches of experimental psychology, human-computer interaction, human factors, or related field).
• Special knowledge or skills that would be valuable:
o Comfortable speaking in front of groups with authority.
o Experience moderating research sessions involving groups of participants, such as focus groups, workshops, playtests, or other qualitative research activities.
o Excellent organizational and communication skills.
o Comfortable with Office 365 tools, survey/data analysis tools, and databases
o Comfortable with using technology, setting up lab hardware, and troubleshooting common device connectivity issues.
o Knowledge of research design, qualitative, and quantitative methodologies.
o Familiar with game design theory and development process for video games.
o Able to adapt and learn quickly when faced with a large variety of problems.
o Genuinely enjoy gaming in all forms!

_ Nice to haves:

• Experience using AI-powered transcription tools to convert video and audio recordings into accurate, searchable text for research, analysis, or documentation purposes.
• Experience designing, configuring, or deploying custom agents using Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, or similar AI platforms to automate workflows, support research activities, or solve business challenges.
• Familiarity with quantitative research methods, including data collection, statistical analysis, interpretation of results, and reporting of insights.
• Experience troubleshooting PC or console hardware, software, or game build issues to ensure successful execution of playtests and a high-quality participant experience.
• Demonstrated ability to learn new technologies and research tools quickly and apply them effectively in a fast-paced environment.

jobs.title: Case Manager
jobs.description:
Overview

Case Manager

Samaritan Daytop Village operates transitional housing programs for single adults and families experiencing homelessness across all five boroughs of New York City. The Case Manager works directly with clients to conduct interviews, evaluate their needs, and collaboratively develop Independent Living Plans. This includes identifying and leveraging community resources, coordinating referrals to services such as healthcare, education, and legal support, and assisting clients in relocating to permanent housing. The role also involves maintaining detailed documentation, monitoring client progress, and advocating on their behalf to help remove barriers to stability and self-sufficiency.

Responsibilities

Build professional relationships with clients and maintain confidentiality
Review client eligibility documents and explore non-shelter alternatives
Create and manage client files and records
Conduct intake interviews and psycho-social assessments
Develop and update Independent Living Plans with short- and long-term goals
Refer clients to permanent housing and community-based services
Support clients in overcoming barriers and advocating for themselves
Track client progress and document updates through regular contact
Follow up with clients and referral agencies to monitor service outcomes
Provide data for required reports (weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual)
Act as a liaison with outside organizations for education, healthcare, childcare, housing, and legal matters

Qualifications

High School Diploma or equivalent required; Associate or Bachelor’s Degree in Human Services, Social Work, or a related field strongly preferred
At least 1 year of experience in case management or social services working with individuals experiencing homelessness, substance use, mental health challenges, or other complex needs
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build trust with individuals from diverse backgrounds
Clear and effective communication skills for conducting interviews, documenting progress, and coordinating with external partners
Ability to maintain accurate records and meet reporting deadlines
Commitment to maintaining client confidentiality and adhering to professional ethics
Familiarity with New York City’s housing, healthcare, legal, childcare, and educational resources
Problem-solving skills and a supportive approach to helping clients overcome challenges
Organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple responsibilities
Culturally sensitive and responsive to the needs of individuals and families experiencing homelessness

Additional Information

The Case Manager role is a full-time non-exempt role with an hourly rate of $25.21 (annualized at 35 hours a week to $45,895) with a full benefits package. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance, 25 days of paid time off, access to a retirement account with an employer to match, and tuition reimbursement.

This role is located in Morris Heights, Bronx and has a schedule of Sunday-Thursday 8am-4pm.

jobs.description:
BACKGROUND INFORMATION:

The Center for Community Health (CCH) represents an exciting opportunity for Tulsa. The goal is to improve health disparities in the Tulsa community, decrease re-admission rates and inappropriate emergency room usage, and increase the use of primary care providers to improve Saint Francis Health System (SFHS) patient health outcomes.

POSITION SUMMARY:

Provides services to bridge the gap between Center for Community Health clients and community health services by: Coordinating referrals to community agencies for additional assistance, treatment, and continuity of care. Completes electronic documentation of each client contact. CMs will work closely with medical providers and primary case management teams at SFHS, Laureate, and other agencies to improve client care and outcomes. CMs will primarily work out of SHFS patient rooms and have office space at SFHS and/or Laureate. CMs will implement effective strategies for linking high risk uninsured and underinsured clients to primary care/medical homes; increase access to appropriate health care and community-based services; assist individuals in improving health status; and promote behavior change in using the health care delivery system.
Principal Duties and Responsibilities/Essential Job Functions
The following functions represent most of the duties performed by the position but are not meant to be all-inclusive or prevent other duties from being assigned when necessary.
ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS (95% of Time):

Build trust and rapport with high-risk patients through bedside screening and engagement in hospital, emergency department, and behavioral health inpatient settings.
Provide focused case management by linking enrolled clients to the most appropriate venue for entry into the health care delivery system to include addressing the social determinants of health: transportation, primary care provider, food, utilities, health insurance, medications, housing, domestic violence, and access to internet, phone, and identity.
Coordinate care with SFHS physicians, case management, and other staff to provide coordinated screening for referred patients.Work with a multidisciplinary health care provider team. Participate in weekly meetings and visit identified patients in the hospital before discharge.
Coordinate as needed with Tulsa Health Department (THD) services and community partner resources.
Engage clients through home visits and meet clients in community-based settings such as shelters, hospitals, clinics, and partner agency sites, to deliver outreach, support care coordination, and address social determinants of health.
Participate in and attend regularly scheduled supervision meetings; be prepared to share both successes and pitfalls of case management.
Provide culturally and linguistically appropriate services to assigned clients.
Maintain complete and accurate documentation of all activities and reports through computerized data entry in accordance with program standards, guidelines and THD requirements. This includes preparing and submitting paperwork, such as, Workflow List, Enrollment Questionnaires, Client Summaries, and Weekly Caseload List.
Attend regular peer group meetings for networking and information sharing for optimal care management and navigation.
Other duties as assigned including those required to fulfill activities in support of public health emergency operations.

SECONDARY JOB FUNCTIONS (5% of Time):

Participate in staff meetings, quality assurance activities, and in-service trainings.
Complete monthly time sheet and mileage forms.

Qualifications/Specifications/Knowledge and Skills
Education:
Bachelor’s degree required. Health care, social work, or public health background or education preferred.
Experience:
One-year experience in health care, social work, or public health preferred. Previous experience with low-income individuals and engaging culturally diverse individuals in health and social services is preferred.
Knowledge and Skills:

Bilingual in English/Spanish is required.

Must have ability to work quietly and respectfully in a shared workspace.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills are required to provide effective health counseling and obtain cooperation from individuals who come from a wide range of economic, social, and ethnic backgrounds.
Demonstrated comfort working in hospital and behavioral health settings and interacting with individuals experiencing physical, behavioral, or mental health challenges.
Skill in operating a personal computer and smart phone applications.
Understanding of healthcare delivery processes.
Skills in obtaining and protecting personal health information (PHI).
Effective interpersonal skills in working with personnel at all organizational levels.

Licenses/Certification:

Valid Oklahoma driver’s license required

Supplemental Information
INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL WORKING RELATIONSHIPS:

Regular internal contact with various nurses and case managers to coordinate care or referrals for patients.
External contact with community partners for the coordination of care and referrals for clients.

PHYSICAL EFFORT:

Requires frequent mobility throughout a high-volume hospital environment, including travel between patient rooms, clinical units, and multiple floors.
Ability to visit clients’ homes, conduct interviews, attend meetings, sit for extended periods, and pick up and deliver transportable medical equipment, ie. briefs, shower chairs, wheelchairs, etc.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY/ACCOUNTABILITY:

Direct Supervision – None
Indirect Supervision – None
Budget/Money/Material – Responsible for assigned computer hardware and software
Reports to – Manager, Center for Community Health
Location – St Francis Health System

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Exposure to hospital environments and individuals with physical, behavioral, or mental health challenges; must follow safety and infection‑control procedures.
Exposure to stressful or emotionally charged situations common in healthcare settings.
Performs additional work in office spaces at SFHS/Laureate and in community locations such as homes, shelters, and partner sites.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS:

Must maintain THD record confidentiality according to HIPAA regulations.
Must possess ability and willingness to perform job-related travel

FLSA Status:
Non-Exempt

Benefits:

We offer a complete benefits package to full-time employees including health care, dental, vision, retirement, deferred compensation plans, flexible spending accounts, life insurance, long-term disability, holidays, and paid time off.

Part-time employees who work an average of 20 hours per week over the course of a year, receive benefits on a pro-rated basis.

Job Details

Description

FULL DESCRIPTION

If you believe healthcare is a right, that everyone deserves high quality care so they can enjoy their highest level of health and wellbeing, and you value each person's individual story – consider joining us at Neighborhood!

As a community health worker (CHW), you’ll have an important role in creating a positive experience for patients at Neighborhood.

About The Role

You’ll listen with kindness to patients’ concerns, seek solutions, and assist patients and families with navigating services and community resources. Responsibilities include:

Consults with providers regarding patient needs for referrals or linkages and assist patients in accessing and completing referrals.
Assists patients in accessing community resources such as food pantries, clothing, shelter, transportation, education, parenting or other services as referred by providers.
Assist patients in completing healthcare forms such as applications for Medicaid, Child and Family Health Plus and Sliding Fee Scale program. Connect patients to facilitated enrollers.
Obtains prior authorizations as needed. Documents and tracks referrals until completion.
Conducts community outreach to identify people who are experiencing homelessness and educates them about health needs.
Supports people who are experiencing homelessness in accessing healthcare services at Neighborhood.
Serves as health and community resources coordinator for patients and providers.
Advocates for patients with community agencies and services.
Conducts outreach and speaks to community groups.
Assists in developing Neighborhood staff to improve patient navigation, decrease barriers for patients in accessing care and connect patients to care.

You will be primarily based at our Blasdell location, 4233 Lake Avenue, Blasdell.

What It’s Like To Work At Neighborhood

The top three words employees say describe the work environment are: teamwork, supportive, kind
. These are from an anonymous survey of Neighborhood employees for the Buffalo Business First Best Places to Work competition. Neighborhood earned “finalist” distinction in the competition for four consecutive years. We are a group of flexible and kind individuals who are open to each other’s ideas and see opportunities to innovate and find solutions when challenges arise.

Education And Skills

High school diploma
Experience in community health, patient resource coordination or equivalent experience
Medical office and medical terminology knowledge and experience preferred
Attention to detail and follow-through, organizational and influencing skills
Experience with Electronic Health Records (EHRs), Microsoft Office Suite, and other computer software
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Kindness: you treat each person with respect and compassion, valuing each person’s story
Resiliency: you see opportunities to innovate and find solutions when challenges arise
Teamwork: you are open to others’ unique perspectives, and will collaborate to meet shared goals

Must be available to work Monday-Friday between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., and have ability to travel for community outreach and work extended hours once a week 7:00-9:00 p.m.

What We Offer

Compensation: $22.25 an hour based on a full-time, 40-hour workweek

Benefits: You’ll have options for medical, dental, life, and supplemental insurance. We also offer a 403b match, health savings accounts with employer contribution, wellbeing programs, continuing education opportunities, generous paid time off, and holidays.

About Neighborhood:
Neighborhood Health Center is the largest and longest serving Federally Qualified Health Center in Western New York and is the highest ranked health center for quality in the region. We provide primary and integrated healthcare services all under one roof, regardless of a person’s ability to pay. Services include internal/family medicine, pediatrics, OB-GYN, dentistry, podiatry, psychiatry, vision care, nutrition and behavioral health counseling, and pharmacy services. We’re working toward a Western New York where all enjoy their highest level of health and wellbeing.

Neighborhood Health Center is an equal opportunity employer.

Right at Home West Palm Beach & Vero Beach

Connecting clients, caregivers, families, and Right at Home through trust,

communication, and exceptional care.

It begins with trust.

It begins with relationships.

It begins with having someone who listens, follows through, and makes sure the right

people are connected at the right time.

That’s where you come in.

We’re looking for a Care Manager
who understands that great home care is about

much more than scheduling caregivers and completing assessments. It’s about creating

a strong connection between our clients, their families, our caregivers, and the Right at

Home team.

The Care Manager is a trusted liaison between the people we serve and the agency

that serves them—someone who can listen to a client’s concerns, recognize

opportunities to improve care, support our caregivers, and make sure important

information doesn’t fall through the cracks.

You’ll be involved from the beginning of the client relationship, conducting initial

assessments and helping families understand how Right at Home can support them.

You’ll stay connected as care evolves, monitor important reports and outcomes, and

help ensure our clients receive the quality, consistency, and responsiveness they

deserve.

You’ll also play an important role in developing and supporting our caregivers—from

conducting new-hire orientations to helping them understand what it means to represent

Right at Home in a client’s home.

If you’re someone who enjoys people, thrives on organization and accountability,

communicates exceptionally well, and takes pride in making things better, we’d love to

meet you.

What You’ll Do

Your responsibilities will include:

 Serve as a primary liaison
between clients, families, caregivers, and the Right

at Home team, ensuring concerns, questions, and important information are

communicated and addressed promptly.

 Conduct initial client assessments
and help develop an understanding of each

client’s needs, preferences, goals, and home environment.

 Build strong client relationships
through regular communication, follow-up,

responsiveness, and a genuine commitment to their experience.

 Conduct new-hire orientations
and help new caregivers understand Right at

Home’s expectations, culture, policies, procedures, and commitment to quality

care.

 Regularly review RightAssist reports,
identify trends, concerns, opportunities,

and follow-up items, and communicate findings to the appropriate members of

the leadership team.

 Manage and support the Guide Program
, ensuring clients and caregivers

receive the appropriate guidance, resources, communication, and follow-through.

 Assist with HR activities,
including onboarding, documentation, employee

Communication, And Other Administrative Responsibilities As Needed.

 Support caregiver engagement and accountability
, helping caregivers feel

connected, informed, and supported while maintaining high standards of care

and professionalism.

 Identify and communicate changes in client needs
, caregiver performance,

scheduling concerns, service issues, or other matters that may impact the quality

of care.

 Participate in client and caregiver follow-up
, helping resolve issues before

they become larger problems.

 Collaborate with the scheduling, operations, recruiting, and leadership

teams
to ensure everyone is working from the same information and toward the

same goal.

 Help create a culture of exceptional service
, where clients feel heard,

caregivers feel valued, and families know they have a responsive team behind

them.

 Represent Right at Home professionally
with clients, families, caregivers,

referral partners, and members of the community.

Who You Are

You’re someone who naturally builds relationships and enjoys helping people.

You’re a strong communicator who can listen carefully, ask thoughtful questions, and

handle difficult conversations with professionalism and empathy.

You’re organized, proactive, and comfortable managing multiple priorities without losing

sight of the people behind the paperwork, reports, and responsibilities.

You notice details.

You follow through.

You don’t wait for someone else to solve a problem when you can take ownership and

help make it better.

You understand that exceptional home care depends on communication, consistency,

accountability, and trust.

You’re comfortable working with both people and processes
—whether that means

conducting a client assessment, orienting a new caregiver, reviewing a report, following

up with a family, or assisting the HR team.

Most importantly, you genuinely care about older adults and the families who trust us to

help them remain safe, independent, and comfortable at home.

Experience in home care, healthcare, senior services, care coordination, case

management, human resources, nursing, social services, or another client-facing

healthcare environment
is highly valued.

Home care experience is helpful, but not required. We’ll teach you our systems and our

business.

We’re looking for someone who already knows how to build trust, communicate

effectively, take ownership, and make things happen.

Why This Role Matters

Every day, you’ll have the opportunity to make a difference—not just in the lives of our

clients, but also in the lives of the caregivers who care for them.

You’ll help connect the dots.

You’ll help solve problems.

You’ll help our team stay accountable.

And you’ll help make sure that the Right at Home experience is one that clients,

families, and caregivers can trust.

If that sounds like the kind of work you’re meant to do, we’d love to hear from

you.

Compensation: $20.00 - $28.00 per hour

Right at Home’s mission is simple...to improve the quality of life for those we serve. We accomplish this by providing the Right Care, and we deliver this brand promise each and every day around the world. However, we couldn’t do it without having the Right People. Our care teams are passionate about serving our clients and are committed to providing the personal care and attention of a friend, whenever and wherever it is needed.

That’s where you come in. At Right at Home, we help ordinary people who have a passion to serve others become extraordinary care team members. We seek to find people who are compassionate, empathetic, reliable, determined and are focused on improving the quality of life for others.

To our care team members, we commit to deliver the following experiences when you partner with Right at Home:

Our Company

StepStone Family & Youth Services

Overview

StepStone Family & Youth Services provides trauma informed, youth centered services to children and families involved in foster care. The Foster Care Case Manager plays a vital role in supporting children, youth, and foster families through individualized case management, advocacy, and service coordination that promotes safety, stability, permanency, and overall well-being.

We are seeking a compassionate and dedicated Foster Care Case Manager who is passionate about supporting children and families through trauma informed, strengths based, and family centered practices. This role is ideal for a professional who builds strong relationships, advocates for the needs of youth, and works collaboratively to help children and families navigate the foster care system successfully.

The Foster Care Case Manager is responsible for coordinating and monitoring services, developing individualized case plans, conducting regular visits, maintaining timely and accurate documentation, and supporting placement stability. This position collaborates closely with foster parents, biological families, schools, referral agencies, community providers, and multidisciplinary treatment teams to ensure youth receive the resources and support necessary to achieve positive outcomes.

The ideal candidate is compassionate, organized, adaptable, and solutions focused, with a strong commitment to providing high quality, trauma informed services that empower youth and families and promote safety, permanency, stability, and long term success.

Responsibilities

Receives/responds to incoming calls from referral sources/potential clients and exchanges information to identify the clients' needs and consults with Director of Clinical Management to determine the Company's ability to meet them.
Completes all viable referrals by setting up and carrying out pre-screening assessments, completion of pre-screening reports, and preparation of case proposals and other related pre-admission paperwork (i.e., obtains authorization for payment, coordinates availability of an appropriate treatment team).
Oversees, directs and supervises field staff assigned in assisting with pre-screening process.
Accesses national/state/company account information, including the account names and terms of contracts or other past payer agreements, as appropriate.
Consults with third party representatives regarding client benefit coverage, client financial responsibility, company service authorization and specific reimbursement procedures. Presents company’s services, interprets potential reimbursement options and negotiates reimbursement levels with third party payer.
Contacts referral sources to advise them of case acceptance and provides information on the clinical team responsible for client's case.
Develops/maintains a working knowledge of all services/resources provided by the Company and services available within the community. Assists in identifying alternative community service sources when company solutions are not appropriate or available.
Maintains relationships with standard referral sources and payer case managers. Contacts identified referral sources and seeks referrals as appropriate. Records outcome of calls and keeps the SAR informed.
Monitors/tracks referral sources' satisfaction levels, tracks/reports on conversion ratios and provides summary reports to management at requested intervals.
Implements/maintains, with the up line management, operational processes to ensure compliance with Company policies, requirements and regulatory mandates.
Adheres to and participates in Company’s mandatory HIPAA privacy program/practices and Business Ethics and Compliance programs.
Participates in quarterly growth planning meetings/activities including discussions around staffing and recruitment needs.
Participates in special projects and performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a human services field or nursing field.
Valid driver's license.
Must have two years of experience with case management or related discipline
Must be able to communicate both verbally and in writing.

About Our Line Of Business

StepStone Family and Youth Services, an affiliate of BrightSpring Health Services, provides the full spectrum of support to children in need of alternative, safer, and more positive living environments with residential and family services. StepStone connects children and youth who need homes with foster families, as well as foster care training, respite care and support services. For young adults transitioning from foster care to independent living, StepStone provides personalized guidance and training on basic life skills, including money management and education. jobs.description:
Site: Mass General Brigham Community Physicians, Inc.

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.

Job Summary

Across the country, governments, employers, and American families have struggled in the face of rising healthcare costs. Efforts historically have targeted narrow programs and patient populations, and while many have succeeded, healthcare costs continue to rise. It’s time to take a radically different approach. A new approach involves putting the patient at the center with the goals of improving value and providing better outcomes at lower cost for patients. The Population Health Management (PHM) department at Mass General Brigham is charged with the challenge to drive better value for patients across Mass General Brigham. To achieve its goals, PHM leverages financial and clinical data to examine opportunities, designs and delivers innovative care models using product development and design thinking disciplines, and leverages problem solving, teamwork, and leadership skills to drive ongoing improvement.

As an integral member of the Population Health Management Operations team, The Transition of Care Nurse Care Manager provides episodic care management for Medicare Shared Savings Program (MSSP) and Medicaid ACO patients from inpatient admission to home. This includes follow up phone calls after discharge, medication reconciliation, and ensuring patient has appropriate follow up appointments scheduled as well as documenting and ensuring all billing requirements are met prior to submitting TCM charges. The Transition of Care Nurse Manager directly interfaces with patients (via phone), Primary Care physicians, pharmacists, care managers, and health care teams involved in patient care as well collaborating with PHM Clinical Operations leadership.

Primary Responsibilities

Manages episodic transitions of care for Medicare Risk and Medicaid risk patients from inpatient discharge to home as applicable.
Calls all discharged patients within two business days of discharge and conducts post discharge assessments.
Works alongside the PHM Clinical Pharmacist to identify and perform Medication Reconciliation for identified patients within the two day follow up phone call.
Reviews discharge instructions/paperwork prior to call to review with patient any action items needed prior to follow up appointment.
Facilitate face to face follow-up appointment with their PCP within 7-14 days after discharge (or according to discharge instructions if applicable).
Document patient interaction (phone calls) in the appropriate patient chart in the electronic medical record.
Manages and coordinates transitions of care by communicating the care plan to other providers and care managers and applicable practice staff.
Maintains all documentation according to standards and requirements.

Demonstrates effective teamwork and collaboration with the primary care provider and the care team
Engages the patient and caregiver as active members of the care team and facilitates an organized and effective, warm hand off for transitions of care back to the patient's medical home (PCP).
Participates in regular meetings with the providers and the care team to identify opportunities for better transitions or to modify workflows as needed.
Communicates with other PHM and (Regional Service Operation (RSO) departments and sites to foster collaboration as a 'system' around the patients served.

Organizational Responsibilities

Demonstrates a positive attitude in dealing with patients, co-workers, and other health care providers and in addressing problems and/or crisis situations.
Requires the ability to work independently as well as function effectively within a team-based model of care.
Able to establish collegial relationships with physicians, office staff and health care providers in physician's offices, community agencies, hospitals, and other health care facilities.
Functioning within the patient centered model of care, demonstrates a commitment to meeting the patient’s needs and expectations.
Functioning within the team-based model of care
Demonstrates initiative and creativity to continuously improve services, work processes, and other activities that affect quality and utilization.
Follows applicable policies and procedures for general safety, fire safety, infection control, attendance, punctuality, and appearance.
Performs all duties as assigned.

Other Duties And Responsibilities

Assumes accountability for professional growth and development.
Acts as a role model for patients by practicing behaviors consistent with the program goals of health promotion and disease prevention.
Identifies quality of care issues and reports the concerns to the appropriate person.
Collects, prepares, and reports data as directed.
Assists in preparation for external audits and surveys as applicable.

Associate’s Degree Nursing (ASN) or Bachelor’s Degree Nursing (BSN).

jobs.description:
Elder Care Coordinator Wanted:
Detail-Obsessed, Big-Hearted, Ready to Make a Real Difference: Salunga, PA | On-Site with travel | Join a team where we believe no one should have to age alone.
SIGN-ON BONUS- $3,000 AVAILABLE

Ready for a job where the work you do actually changes someone's day, sometimes their whole week? This is it.
This is a hands-on role based in Salunga, PA, part office, part out in the community. You'll split your time between focused work at the office and visiting clients, sitting in on care plan meetings at senior living communities, and showing up as the steady, trusted person a senior can count on when they have no one else to turn to. If you love variety and human connection in your workday, this is built for you.
As an Elder Care Coordinator, you're the glue. You make sure nothing- not a bill, not a deadline, not a detail- slips through the cracks. You'll keep client accounts paid on time and reconciled to the penny, and you'll be the go-to voice for senior living communities and healthcare providers whenever a client needs someone in their corner. Yes, it's detail-driven work, but every number you get right and every call you make is really about protecting someone who is counting on you, often someone who has no one else to do it. That's what makes it exciting: the stakes are real, and so is the impact.
And you're never out there alone. Every fiduciary decision is backed by Pam Witwer, our Founder and Fiduciary of Record. You own the day-to-day with sharp instincts and good judgment, and you know exactly when to loop her in. If you're the kind of person who spots the discrepancy nobody else would catch, and who can bring calm and clarity to a vulnerable person on a hard day, we want to talk to you.
Bonus is $1,000 after a 90-day positive performance review and $2,000 after one year of continuous employment with a positive performance evaluation

Compensation:
$52,000 annually

Responsibilities:
Case Management:

Track and pay client bills on schedule, monitor accounts, and reconcile statements monthly

Prepare contracts and onboard accepted clients; conduct in-person signings when it best serves the client

Serve as primary liaison to senior living communities and healthcare providers; attend care plan meetings and conduct regular client visits

Coordinate healthcare logistics and escalate every clinical, financial, and legal matter to the Fiduciary of Record, without exception

Maintain the complete client record and deliver a written weekly case report

Business Development:

Build and maintain referral relationships with elder law attorneys, financial advisors, and senior living communities

Represent LPES at networking events and deliver presentations at senior centers

Cultivate qualified referrals and route them into intake — you build the relationship, Pam makes the accept/decline call

Support special projects assigned by Pam or Operations Manager Ron Wybraniec

Qualifications:
Extensive experience in senior services or the elder care sector

Demonstrated ability to build professional relationships and represent an organization in the community

Financial literacy and comfort with bookkeeping, reconciliation, and online banking, or the aptitude to learn them quickly. Training provided

Strong ethical standards and the discipline to operate inside a defined authority boundary, including knowing when to stop and escalate

Excellent written and verbal communication, and a professional presence appropriate to attorneys, facility administrators, families, and public audiences

Comfort with AI tools, Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, the LPES CRM, and the Quo phone application. Training provided on LPES systems

Valid driver's license, current auto insurance, and a reliable personal vehicle. Mileage reimbursed

Successful completion of a background check and credit check

About Company

Lancaster PA Executor Services (LPES) is a small, independent fiduciary firm serving seniors and families across central and south-central Pennsylvania with Financial Power of Attorney, Healthcare Power of Attorney, Executor, Trustee, and estate support services. Founded in 2024 by Pam Witwer after 30+ years in public service, LPES fills a critical gap for families who need compassionate, professional fiduciary support but can't afford traditional attorney-level fees. 
The team works collaboratively with elder law attorneys and healthcare providers, often stepping in during a family's most overwhelming moments — where trust, discretion, and precision matter as much as compassion.

jobs.title: Grants Coordinator
jobs.description:
The Grants Coordinator plays a critical role in sustaining and growing Youth Guidance’s public-sector funding by coordinating the administration, reporting, compliance, and infrastructure associated with government grants. The position maintains systems and deadlines, coordinates cross-functional grant reporting, supports public funding prospect research, and assists with the development and writing of government grant proposals, applications, reports, and other funder materials. The role also helps ensure Youth Guidance meets funder requirements, submits high-quality and timely materials, and maximizes public funding opportunities.

Approximately 80% of the role is dedicated to the administration, reporting, compliance, coordination, and writing support associated with government grants from city, county, state, and federal sources. This may include drafting or contributing to grant applications, proposals, reports, and other funder materials in partnership with the Director of Government Funding & Partnerships and other internal stakeholders. The remaining time (less than 20%) provides administrative and project support to External Affairs staff and leadership in advancing broader fundraising and engagement priorities.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities:

Grant Administration & Reporting
• Maintain a comprehensive calendar of public grant application and reporting deadlines
• Oversee entry of deadlines, files, and reporting metrics of all government, federal, and state grants into Salesforce and other platforms as needed.
• Maintain accurate records of government grant portal credentials for application and reporting purposes
• Collaborate with the Evaluation and Quality Improvement (EQI) team to gather quantitative data and complete funder reports
• Create and maintain reporting infrastructure with program leadership and staff to gather qualitative data for reporting.
• Work with the Finance team to secure financial data and prepare financial reports
• Facilitate and submit required reports and documentation in partnership with program, evaluation, and finance staff.
• Support Compliance Officer with tasks related to program audits and accreditation.
• Maintain a library of agency documents and data necessary for desk audits.
• Create and maintain an organized library of agency documents and program Memoranda of Understanding that can be tailored to specific schools and/or districts.
• Monitor progress of funding proposals post-submission to ensure compliance with all required procedures and deadlines.

Grant Prospecting and Writing
• Research and identify public funding opportunities at the city, county, state, and federal levels.
• Draft and contribute to government grant applications, proposals, reports, and other funder materials in coordination with the Director of Government Funding & Partnerships and program, evaluation, and finance staff.

Team & Administrative Support
• Provide administrative support to the External Affairs team staff and leadership as needed.
• Maintain accurate and timely public funding opportunity, award, deadline, and reporting information in Salesforce and other relevant systems.
• Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Education/Experience/Training
• Bachelor’s degree required, or equivalent relevant experience.
• At least 2-3 years of experience in project management, grant administration, or high-level administrative work.
• Experience with writing and coordinating government or philanthropic grants strongly preferred; related nonprofit or government internship experience will also be considered.

Skills/Abilities
• Highly organized, detail-oriented, and capable of strategic thinking.
• Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, work under pressure and consistently meet deadlines.
• Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to represent the agency effectively to external funders and stakeholders.
• Collaborative team player who works well independently and across departments.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite required; experience with Salesforce or other CRM database system preferred.

Benefits
Youth Guidance offers a competitive benefit package for eligible full-time employees including the option to participate in medical, dental, and vision plans as well as short-term disability, life insurance, flex spending accounts, pet insurance, 401k, a wellness program and more. You may also qualify for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF).

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
Program Manager
, Brooklyn, New York 
In-Person Work Required  
This is an exempt position and is not eligible for overtime 

WHO WE ARE  

Explore Schools is a network of public charter schools providing 1,700 students in Brooklyn with the outstanding education they deserve. Our goal is to provide students with curriculum and instruction that is both standards-aligned and culturally responsive. Our approach is designed to provide the conditions that nurture students as critical thinkers and natural problem-solvers.  As an organization we are committed to engaging in work that disrupts and roots out systems and structures that perpetuate white supremacy. We intentionally seek to build and maintain a diverse and talented team that reflects the backgrounds and experiences of our students and creates an inclusive environment for all employees.  

WHAT WE BELIEVE 

We believe that all children can learn when immersed in a rich environment full of high expectations, rigorous academics, and caring, committed adults. We believe equity and excellence are not mutually exclusive—we can meet the needs of all students in our schools, while actively engaging parents and driving toward excellent academic results. We believe it is both our privilege and responsibility to help close the opportunity gap in the Brooklyn community.  

WHO YOU ARE 

Explore Schools seeks a dedicated school operations professional who excels at project management, and providing high-level support to leaders. You have a combination of experience and interest in providing support and maintaining strong systems for instructional and operational needs. You are extremely detail-oriented, an excellent relationship-builder, and skilled at presenting information to audiences in ways that are easy to digest. The ideal candidate is proficient in Excel and enjoys working in an environment where you get to take initiative and roll up your sleeves. Additionally, you possess the following qualities: 

Dedicated to working in communities that have historically been underserved and under-resourced 

Committed to thoughtfully engaging in identity work necessary to take a culturally responsive approach to pedagogy and relationship-building with students and colleagues 

Strong project manager: proven track record of managing multiple projects, and tracking progress 

Exceptional communication skills: clear and concise delivery with approaches that consider audiences 

Savvy relationship manager: ability to manage up, hold peers and leaders accountable, and motivate others 

Experience working with data: cleaning up and maintaining systems, communicating complex information into easy-to-digest presentations 

Flexible can-do attitude: willingness to provide support as needed, excited to support the instructional team through different ad-hoc projects 

Highly organized, and strong attention to detail 

Excel proficiency; preferred 

A minimum of 3 years of experience, preferred  

Bachelor's degree; required 

WHAT YOU'LL DO  

As a Program Manager, you will work in the Operations team at a school and collaborate closely with leadership to create and enforce strong systems that provide school support and manage assessments and data. This work will include managing broad school operational and instructional projects, as well as providing staff trainings around assessments and data management.  
Collaborate with teachers and instructional leaders to align on operational support needed, maintaining strong relationships 

Implement necessary systems and operational support for the instructional team, communicating clearly and meeting deadlines 

Manage and share scholar data with teachers, leaders, families and students, includes: student information system, performance data (IAs) testing information, assessments, enrollment data, gradebooks, report cards, etc. 

Lead staff training for student information systems, assessments, gradebooks, and student data analysis 

Manage internal and external communication structures, including creating and managing family communication 

Coordinate testing administration, scoring, and data analysis for internal assessments and state exams 

Work with instructional team to create and disperse school schedules 

Manage implementation of digital curriculum and platforms for students and staff 

Additional operational duties: manage special projects, support tech needs, manage field trips, coordinate student transportation, coordinate coverage and substitutes, support student recruitment and enrollment, cover main office, work with parents, lunch/recess duty, other special projects as needed 

Actively engage in identity work and necessary conversations in order to dismantle white supremacy culture 

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS 

Explore Schools staff members receive a competitive salary, paid time off including network shutdown days, considerable matching of retirement contributions, and more.  
The salary range for incoming Program Managers is $60,000 to $85,000. This is our good faith range at the time of posting. 

Incoming salaries are determined based on experience and internal equity.   

Because we value staff members staying in their roles over time, we do not currently cap salary ranges and this is the range for incoming staff members only.   

This is base salary and does not include additional compensation opportunities, such as signing bonuses, additional time worked pay, stipends, leadership opportunities, and additional pay for specialized certifications and advanced degrees.   

Additionally, you can expect: 
A comprehensive benefits plan, covering up to 95% of the cost for employees and their families. Other benefits include dental and vision plans, employer paid disability and life insurance, parental leave benefits, flexible spending account options, generous vacation time and paid holidays, professional development, continuing education scholarships, referral bonuses, employee assistance program (EAP), childcare assistance, a 403(b) retirement plan with employer matching, and more! 

Flexible and reflective leadership: dedicated to staff development, team cohesion, and shared responsibility for decision-making, development, and team-wide priorities  

Driven and passionate colleagues who contribute to a professional and collaborative work environment   

Opportunities to sit on various committees and participate in initiatives central to key organizational decisions and strategic planning   

Our school-based staff also receive:   

Professional development: weekly PD, year-round retreats and trainings, and ongoing coaching by professionals   

Continued education support: staff are eligible to receive scholarship funds towards qualifying certification costs or higher education tuition  

A flexible work environment with the ability to choose your work location during non-student hours 1-3 days a week when possible, all within a structured 45-hour work week. 

LOCATION AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS 

Explore Schools is a network of charter schools located in Canarsie, Crown Heights, and Flatbush communities of Brooklyn, NY. Our schools are currently operating fully in-person. For this position:  
In-person work is required  

This is an exempt position and is not eligible for overtime.  

The standard work week is 45 hours, though at times you may work more.  

This role requires that you be able to stand for at least 5 hours a day, take multiple trips up and down the stairs in a day, and be able to move quickly in an emergency.   

This role also requires that you be able to lift up to 15 pounds. 

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER 

As discussed in our Who We Are section, Explore Schools is an equal opportunity employer. It is important to us that all staff members have a place of employment that is free of discrimination of all kinds and where staff can bring their authentic selves to work. We do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender expression, age, national origin, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, veteran, or military status. If any employee or applicant believes they have been discriminated against, they should let Tiffany Williams know immediately.

jobs.description:
Turn Connections Into Opportunities. Help Change a Young Life.

At My Friend’s House Family and Children Services, Inc. (My Friend’s House)
, we believe every young person deserves to feel safe, supported, encouraged, and hopeful about his future.

Our nonprofit organization provides a home-like environment for boys ages 12–18 in state custody, helping them build confidence, develop life skills, and prepare for successful futures.
We’re seeking a Community Engagement & Development Coordinator
to connect our mission with the people and organizations who can help us make an even greater impact.

If you’re a relationship-builder, creative communicator, and self-motivated professional who enjoys bringing people together around a meaningful cause, this may be the opportunity for you.

What You’ll Do

You’ll serve as a key connection between My Friend’s House and our community—building relationships, increasing awareness, engaging supporters, and developing the resources needed to sustain our mission.
Build and strengthen relationships with donors, businesses, sponsors, churches, civic groups, foundations, and community partners.
Develop and implement fundraising strategies, campaigns, annual giving, sponsorships, and other revenue opportunities.
Identify, research, write, and manage grants, including required reporting.
Cultivate new donors while strengthening relationships with existing supporters.
Create meaningful opportunities for individuals, businesses, and organizations to become involved with our mission.
Recruit and engage volunteers and community groups.
Share our story through donor communications, community outreach, presentations, social media, marketing, and public relations.
Plan and lead fundraising activities, including one major annual fundraising event of up to 500 guests.
Represent My Friend’s House at community events and networking opportunities.
Collaborate with the Executive Director and staff to establish development goals, track progress, and prepare fundraising reports.

Who We’re Looking For

We’re looking for someone who sees relationships as more than contacts on a list
.
You enjoy meeting people, building genuine connections, and helping others discover meaningful ways to get involved. You’re comfortable talking with a donor or business leader, speaking to a community group, writing a compelling grant proposal, coordinating volunteers, or rolling up your sleeves to make an event successful. You’re organized, creative, dependable, and able to take an idea from concept to completion.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, fundraising, marketing, communications, business, public relations, or a related field.
Relevant experience in nonprofit development, fundraising, community engagement, marketing, communications, or a related role.
Experience with donor cultivation, grants, sponsorships, fundraising campaigns, events, or community partnerships.
Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and public-speaking skills.
Strong organizational and project-management abilities.
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with a small, mission-focused team.
Availability for occasional evening and weekend events.
Valid Tennessee driver’s license and ability to successfully complete required background checks.

Why Join My Friend’s House?

Make an impact you can see.
Your work helps provide care, stability, encouragement, experiences, and opportunities for young men who need them.
Build relationships that matter.
You’ll connect people throughout our community with meaningful ways to make a difference.
Bring your ideas.
We welcome creativity and new approaches to partnerships, fundraising, outreach, and community engagement.
Be part of something personal.
We’re a small, dedicated nonprofit team where every person—and every contribution—matters.

Position Details

Full-time | Exempt | Franklin, Tennessee

Reports to the Executive Director. Occasional evening and weekend availability is required for fundraising and community events.

Help Us Build Brighter Futures

If you want to use your skills, creativity, and ability to connect with people for a mission that matters, we’d love to hear from you.

Join My Friend’s House and help us surround the young men we serve with a community that believes in their future.

Please send your cover letter and resume to Tanassa Pillow, Executive Director at tanassa.pillow@myfriendshousetn.org and copy office@myfriendshousetn.org.
