Job Summary

The Department of Human Services (DHS), through its Family Services Administration (FSA), seeks a skilled Program Manager to enhance the effectiveness of the FSA Families Division. FSA provides tailored protective, intervention, and social services to vulnerable adults and families, aiming for risk reduction and self-sufficiency.

The role of the Program Manager has the overall management, direction and coordination of the Career Map program, as well as, the coordination of Contract Providers, FSA/OAS, OD/OCP in providing quality services to families in the program. The incumbent is also directly responsible for monitoring program delivery, tracking and providing technical assistance for FRSP Providers to ensure continuity and quality of services. Additionally, the Program Manager will develop program, policies and procedures, assuring that practices align with District laws and mandates with a high quality of services for families.

About DHS

The mission of the District of Columbia Department of Human Services (DHS) is to provide meaningful and equitable services, supports, and access to resources for District residents to realize their goals. Our approach to preventing homelessness and supporting individuals and/or families experiencing homelessness is focused both on systems-level reforms and on the quality of the programs and supports within that system. These efforts include creating economic opportunity, making our neighborhoods safer, and providing more effective and efficient government services.

Duties And Responsibilities

The incumbent in this position will be responsible for managing, planning, organizing, and supervising the operation of a program(s) and its activities in accordance with the mission and goals of an agency; develops new programs to support the strategic direction of the agency; advises and consults with administration/division managers; meets with appropriate staff to identify and resolve problems or conflicts; makes or recommends final decisions regarding policy, operations, and administrative procedures of the program. Establishes and manages long- and short-term program goals; develops, analyzes, and evaluates new or modified program/management policies, regulations, goals, or objectives. Develops, implements and maintains complex procedures, administrative monitoring practices and controls in order to obtain smooth and effective operation of a program(s); coordinates work activities of the program to prevent delays in required actions or to improve programs or services; identifies, develops and implements departmental goals, objectives, policies, and priorities; determines resource allocation and levels of service according to established policies; plans and writes grant applications and manages grant-funded projects.

Develops and analyzes program reports; directs the preparation of monthly and annual reports; directs the gathering and analysis of information and reports necessary to document and evaluate processes. Serves as a liaison between the agency and/or division, community agencies, citizen groups, developers, property managers, committees and commissions, federal, state and local agencies, authorities and task forces concerning agency program needs, new programs, policies and procedures and to facilitate progress on specific projects.

jobs.description:
Overview

Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center is an independent, nonprofit organization providing adult cancer treatment and groundbreaking research focused on cancer and infectious diseases. Based in Seattle, Fred Hutch is the only National Cancer Institute-designated cancer center in Washington.

With a track record of global leadership in bone marrow transplantation, HIV/AIDS prevention, immunotherapy and COVID-19 vaccines, Fred Hutch has earned a reputation as one of the world’s leading cancer, infectious disease and biomedical research centers. Fred Hutch operates eight clinical care sites that provide medical oncology, infusion, radiation, proton therapy and related services, and network affiliations with hospitals in five states. Together, our fully integrated research and clinical care teams seek to discover new cures to the world’s deadliest diseases and make life beyond cancer a reality.

At Fred Hutch we value collaboration, compassion, determination, excellence, innovation, integrity and respect. Our mission is directly tied to the humanity, dignity and inherent value of each employee, patient, community member and supporter. Our commitment to learning across our differences and similarities make us stronger. We seek employees who bring different and innovative ways of seeing the world and solving problems.

The clinical research Data Coordinator II
is a member of the Phase I Clinical Trial Program that supports oncology clinical trials conducted at the Fred Hutch/University of Washington Cancer Consortium. The position is responsible for collecting and abstracting clinical data from medical records and research charts, ensuring data quality and timeliness. The team supports a large and diverse portfolio of clinical trials and this position will work in close collaboration with faculty, providers and research staff across multiple disease areas. This position must be able to work independently on multiple research projects, demonstrate attention to detail and strong organizational skills.

Responsibilities

Work with the research team and providers to collect, abstract, and code complex clinical data and information from multiple sources (medical records, research records, etc.) for research subjects.
Code and record said information into various study-specific electronic data-capture systems.
Resolve and answer data queries with minimal errors.
Maintain databases for research studies.
Follow complex instructions for processing laboratory samples (including tumor tissue samples) for tracking, storage, or shipping.
Demonstrate understanding of research study operational flow.
Assist with development of study-specific or program data acquisition forms.
Partner with research coordinator and/or sponsor representatives to review and correct data recorded in the case report forms.
Request medical records from outside medical facilities.
Track and maintain research subject schedules based on complex protocol-specific requirements, and work with clinic staff support services and research team members to ensure subject research assessments are planned for required/appropriate time points.
May interact with research subjects, study team members, or sponsor contacts in order to obtain and submit required study data and for resolution of study-specific queries.
Additional duties as assigned.

Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

BA/BS, RRA (Registered Records Administrator), ART (Accredited Records Technician), or two year degree in the medical field.
Two years of experience in medical records, cancer registry, or related field.
Strong computer skills and experience working with databases.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Medical terminology.

Preferred Qualifications

Strong computer skills and experience with data entry and databases.
Strong attention to detail and ability to multi-task, organize and prioritize multiple projects.
Ability to communicate effectively both verbally and in writing, and to work effectively with colleagues, research subjects, and study sponsor representatives.
Demonstrated ability to work independently, under supervision, and be a team player.
Ability to adapt and respond appropriately to competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

The hourly pay range for this position is from $27.01 to $38.45 and pay offered will be based on experience and qualifications.

Although Fred Hutch is not sponsoring most H-1B visas at this time, candidates who already hold an H-1B sponsored by another organization and are currently in the U.S. may be eligible for this position.

Site: The Brigham and Women's Hospital, Inc.

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.

Job Summary

GENERAL SUMMARY

Overview Statement Rn Care Coordinator (case Manager)

BWH CARE CONTINUUM

The RN Care Coordinator (RNCC) manages a caseload of patients and is responsible for ensuring care that supports desired clinical and financial outcomes. Has the skills and knowledge specific to the unique needs of assigned patients. Coordinating the care prescribed by an interdisciplinary team, the RNCC utilizes patient assessment, care guidelines, protocols, payer regulations and response to therapies to assess the episode of illness from pre admission to post discharge. Participates in the ongoing evaluation of practice patterns and systems and supports efforts to improve quality, cost and satisfaction outcomes. Mobilizes resources to maximize efficiency of care delivery.

Principal Duties And Responsibilities

Care Facilitation Coordinates and insures implementation of the plan of care, utilizing case management principles.
Prior to or within 24-48 hours of admission the RNCC, by interview of the patient/family, discussion with physician team and/or attending MD and other team members, develops a provisional treatment program and tentative discharge date.
Reviews daily treatment plan with physicians, nurses and patient / families to insure interdisciplinary communication and coordination is occurring.
Participates with nursing staff and physicians in patient care rounds to contribute to plan of care and monitor and report patient progress.
Collaborates with other departments to expedite sequencing and scheduling of interventions, consults, treatments and ancillary services.
Provides for daily continuity with patients to assure patient needs related to discharge are met.
Incorporates knowledge of utilization management principles and payer contracts into patient plans of care. Keeps physicians and nurses informed of implications.
Presents alternatives to inpatient stay to attending MD, team and patient / family based on assessed patient level of care and insurance benefits.
Seeks assistance and/or consultation from Care Coordination leadership with plans for outlier and potential or actual resource intensive patients.
Interacts with internal and external health care providers to facilitate patient care including post discharge services.
Contributes to the development, implementation and monitoring of practice guidelines.
Identifies attending, resident and nurse learning needs related to case management and works with service leaders to develop educational plan.
Discharge Planning

Coordinates and executes the discharge planning process for patients, ensuring each patient has a discharge plan.

Assesses continuing care needs in conjunction with other caregivers.
Coordinates and schedules interdisciplinary meetings with the patient and family regarding discharge needs and plan as appropriate.
Assures patient education consistent with discharge plan has occurred.
Identifies service, treatment and funding options for post-hospital care.
Promotes interdisciplinary patient/family communications and documentation that facilitate discharge planning striving to finalize plans the day prior to discharge.
Performs patient/family follow-up after discharge to monitor and support desired outcomes.
Initiates contact with home health agencies and extended care facilities to insure prompt and effective transition of care.
Utilization Management

Collaborates with appropriate individuals, departments, and payers to insure appropriateness of admission, continued days of stay, and reimbursement.

Identifies patients who are likely to have unmet insurance and resource needs and communicates with and/or makes referrals to other members of the health care team and other appropriate departments.
Communicates as needed with third party payers regarding patient’s progress with treatment plan.
Identifies need for and issues Medicare notices of non-coverage, providing appropriate documentation of the process and communication to patient/family and other members of the health care team.
Utilizing industry accepted utilization and/or medical management criteria (InterQual) identifies, monitors and reports variances from established treatment plan, including appropriateness of admission, continued stay, delays in treatment, and discharge plan.
Conducts documented utilization reviews to insurers or intermediaries.
Identifies SNF and AND days for Medicare and Medicaid patients.
Initiates actions concurrently to reduce and/or eliminate inappropriate hospital admissions and days, and system delays.
Works with payers and physicians to concurrently address level of care concerns effecting claims and reimbursement.
Contributes to utilization and practice improvement efforts by reviewing reports with colleagues and providing feedback on utilization trends and payer issues.
Serves as the primary patient information source to third party payers.

Qualifications

QUALIFICATIONS Qualifications

Education: Graduate of an approved school of nursing with current registration in Massachusetts. For newly licensed nurses a Bachelor of Science Degree in Nursing is required.

5+ years of acute care experience required

Skills/ Abilities/ Competencies Required

1 year of inpatient acute case management experience required

Skills and Abilities Previous experience in a hospital or health care setting; bilingual (English/Spanish) preferred; strong clinical assessment skills; excellent interpersonal skills including ability to work collaboratively and cooperatively within a team and with internal and external customers; strong organizational skill and ability to set priorities; ability to compile data from concurrent and retrospective medical record review to determine clinical appropriateness, able to demonstrate the ability to meet a patient’s needs based on their clinical diagnosis, level of care and discharge plan; ability to negotiate several aspects of care coordination simultaneously; excellent written and verbal communication skills

jobs.title: Patient Care Coordinator - Lansing
jobs.description:
Job Summary
The Patient Care Coordinator is one of the most important roles in the clinic.
You are the person who helps turn a new patient into a scheduled patient, a scheduled patient into a cared-for patient, and a great patient experience into a reason people keep coming back and refer others.
Your role is to:
Keep the clinic moving. Keep patients taken care of. Keep the schedule full.

You will own the front-desk experience, scheduling, patient communication, administrative accuracy, and service education. You will work closely with providers and clinic leadership to remove bottlenecks, solve problems, and create an experience patients remember for the right reasons.
This is not a “sit at the front desk and answer the phone” job. We are looking for someone who takes ownership, sees what needs to be done, and gets it done without waiting to be told.

What You'll Own
1. The Patient Experience
Be the first and last impression patients have of Peak Performance Physical Therapy.
Create a professional, welcoming, and positive experience every time.
Answer questions and solve problems quickly and professionally.
Communicate clearly with patients, providers, referral sources, and teammates.
Make patients feel informed, valued, and taken care of.

2. The Schedule
Own the schedule and help maximize provider availability.
Keep appointments organized, accurate, and filled.
Confirm appointments and proactively reduce avoidable cancellations and no-shows.
Follow up quickly with referrals and new patients to get evaluations scheduled.
Identify open spots and scheduling opportunities before they become lost revenue.
Work with the clinical team to address scheduling challenges and bottlenecks.

3. Patient & Service Education
Help patients understand the services and programs available through Peak Performance.
Clearly explain available options, pricing, scheduling, and next steps.
Identify opportunities to connect patients with additional services that may benefit their overall experience.
Communicate services professionally and ethically while following company policies and applicable healthcare requirements.
Help patients understand the value of continuing their relationship with Peak Performance.

4. Administrative Accuracy
Collect accurate demographic, insurance, referral, and billing information.
Ensure required information is complete before services are provided.
Process patient payments accurately and timely.
Maintain accurate records and documentation.
Complete administrative tasks that keep the clinic running efficiently.
Protect confidential patient information.

5. Clinic Performance
Understand that the front desk has a direct impact on clinic performance.
Look for ways to improve scheduling, patient retention, communication, and efficiency.
Bring problems forward with potential solutions—not just complaints.
Take ownership of assigned responsibilities from start to finish.
Support clinic leadership in achieving operational and patient experience goals.

6. Compliance & Professionalism
Follow HIPAA, privacy requirements, company policies, payer requirements, and applicable laws and regulations.
Maintain patient confidentiality.
Know when an issue needs to be escalated to a provider or leader.
Never provide clinical advice or make treatment decisions outside the scope of the role.
Represent Peak Performance and its values professionally at all times.
Perform other duties as needed to support the success of the clinic.

What We're Looking For
Must Have
High school diploma or equivalent.
Previous customer service, administrative, healthcare, or patient-facing experience.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Strong organizational and multitasking skills.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment.
Strong attention to detail.
Comfortable using computers and scheduling systems.
Ability to handle difficult conversations professionally.
Ability to protect confidential information.
A strong sense of ownership and accountability.

We'd Love to See
Healthcare or physical therapy experience.
Experience with scheduling, insurance, billing, or EMR systems.
Associate's or bachelor's degree.
Customer service or sales experience.
Someone who naturally looks for ways to improve things instead of waiting for someone else to fix them.

The Person Who Wins in This Role
You're probably a great fit if you:
Take ownership.
You don't need someone constantly checking behind you.
Move fast.
You understand that delays cost patients, time, and opportunities.
Notice things.
You see the empty spot on the schedule, the patient who needs a follow-up, and the problem that everyone else missed.
Follow through.
If you say you're going to do something, it gets done.
Communicate.
You don't let problems sit in silence.
Care about the patient.
You understand that great service isn't a script—it's how you make people feel.
Think like an owner.
You understand that great patient care and a healthy business support each other.

Work Environment
Professional outpatient physical therapy clinic.
High level of interaction with patients, providers, and team members.
Fast-paced environment with frequent changes in priorities.
Primarily front-desk and administrative work with regular movement throughout the clinic.

Physical Requirements
Ability to sit and/or stand for extended periods.
Frequent use of computers, phones, and office equipment.
Ability to move throughout the clinic as needed.
Ability to perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

The Bottom Line
If you want a job where you simply check people in and answer phones, this probably isn't it.

If you want to own the patient experience, help build a great clinic, solve problems, keep the schedule moving, and have a measurable impact on the business, we want to talk to you.

Summary:

Energy and Sustainability organization drives the company's clean energy strategy and the reporting that underpins Company's Net Zero commitments. The Clean and Renewable Energy (CaRE) team is hiring a Program Manager on a contingent, limited-term basis. During this period, this role serves as the day-to-day owner and coordinator for Company's energy activity data — the Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 energy datasets that feed the company's greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory, emissions forecasting, and voluntary and regulatory disclosures. This is a hands-on, data-centric role: it requires 3-5 years of experience managing multiple concurrent workstreams in a fast-paced, matrixed environment, direct experience working with large datasets and running or QC'ing analytics, and the ability to communicate data status and insights to technical and non-technical audiences. This individual must have familiarity with corporate GHG accounting and be comfortable with query tools and data QA/validation workflows. This is a full-time, limited-term position.

Responsibilities:
Serve as the day-to-day owner for Company's energy activity data across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 electricity (e.g., FERA, construction energy, network-related electricity, and operational electricity, diesel, natural gas, etc ), from data collection and QA/QC through to the reporting handoff to the Net Zero team
Perform analyses on Company’s Environmental Attribute Certificate (EAC) portfolio and support the development of internal systems to advance portfolio management and modeling.
Run and maintain the recurring data collection, QA/QC, and validation cadence (e.g, quarterly data pulls, follow-ups, YoY analysis) and keeping reporting and analysis on schedule
Perform and QC data pulls from Company's energy data systems, investigate anomalies and data-pipeline issues, and reconcile discrepancies
Coordinate data and process flows across cross-functional partners to maintain accurate and complete inputs from source through to reporting
Support the emissions forecasting cadence as the energy-data point of contact for the Net Zero team, providing and QA'ing the activity data behind regulatory and internal cross-functional forecasts
Develop and maintain program-management artifacts — trackers, roadmaps, status reports, and executive-ready updates — for recurring leadership and cross-functional forums
Support a quarterly reporting cadence (execution updates, exec meeting prep, deck and dashboard creation) using established templates and inputs
Support external assurance and audit activities (e.g., methodology walkthroughs with Company’s assurance provider) and preparing and validating data and documentation as requested
Triage and respond to incoming energy-data and analytical requests; track progress against internal KPIs and stakeholder expectations
Maintain and improve reporting documentation — the what, when, where, how, and why of energy data collection, including team-specific nuances and process flows

Minimum Qualifications:
BA or BS degree in physical sciences, engineering, math, statistics, accounting, business, environment, and/or a sustainability-focused field
3-5 years of experience in program management, data operations, or analytics coordination, ideally supporting technical or data-oriented teams
Direct, hands-on experience working with large datasets — collecting, QA/QC'ing, reconciling, and analyzing data from multiple sources
Familiarity with corporate GHG emissions accounting concepts (Scope 1, 2, and 3) and the activity data that underpins an emissions inventory
Exceptional project-management skills with a demonstrated ability to self-manage complex, data-driven delivery in a fast-paced, matrixed environment
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting data and insights to technical and non-technical audiences and creating graphics for leadership presentations
High-level proficiency in Google Sheets/Excel — advanced formulas, pivot tables, and charts — plus slide/deck creation
Strong attention to detail and accuracy in data work, even under tight deadlines
Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment and comfort with ambiguity

Preferred Qualifications:
Experience with a scripting/query language (e.g., SQL, Python) sufficient to run, automate, or QA data pulls from large data warehouses (e.g., Hive/Presto or equivalent)
Experience building visualizations and dashboards from large, multi-source datasets, particularly with Tableau and Excel
Familiarity with energy/utility data (electricity, natural gas, diesel, and other fuels) and metering/billing data structures
Strong understanding of current practices and trends in greenhouse gas emissions and broader sustainability accounting and reporting
Familiarity with external reporting standards and platforms such as GHGP, CDP, ISSB, GRI, TCFD, SASB, CSRD, etc.
Experience supporting external assurance or audit processes
Experience working within large, matrixed organizations and coordinating across cross-functional partners

jobs.title: Data Analyst - Rollins School of Public Health
jobs.description:
Discover Your Career at Emory University

Emory University is a leading research university that fosters excellence and attracts world-class talent to innovate today and prepare leaders for the future. We welcome candidates who can contribute to the excellence of our academic community.

Description

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Creates and maintains a data dictionary and meta data.
Supports efforts to ensure that data standards are developed and maintained.
Ensures that the uses of data through reports and queries are accurate.
Supports business and system re-engineering and architecture development to define future data needs.
Serves as an organizational consultant on matters relating to databases by providing expertise to assist users in meeting their needs.
Performs other related duties as required.

ADDITIONAL JOB DETAILS:

The research team of Dr. Aaron Siegler (Bio: https://sph.emory.edu/profile/faculty/aaron-siegler) in the Epidemiology Department at Emory University is seeking to hire a Data Analyst to work on several NIH-funded studies in HIV prevention epidemiology and digital health intervention research across local and/or international settings.

These studies include:

Establishing a PrEP Epidemiology, Modeling and Surveillance System (PREMISE), a study to support the development of consistent national HIV Pre-ExposureProphylaxis (PrEP) data to describe its patterns of use, and to understand which programs and policies are effective at facilitating PrEP uptake in the US.
Improving telePrEP initiation and retention outcomes in the US: The MISTR+ study, an NIH-funded series of clinical trials to support the development of low-touchinterventions (such as tailored messaging) and testing their effectiveness on PrEP initiation and retention outcomes.
The Elección (Choice) Cohort: Developing and testing a scalable, platform-agnostic digital intervention in Peru, an NIH-funded clinical trial to improve understanding of the factors associated with HIV acquisition and PrEP uptake; and evaluate the preferences for and effectiveness of an adapted digital health messaging intervention (mHealth) among men in Peru.

The Data Analyst will have the opportunity to work on multiple projects as described above, with specific work distribution depending on experience and interests. The Data Analyst may have the opportunity to contribute to other ongoing projects in Dr. Siegler’s research lab, co-author manuscripts, and present scientific work at national/international scientific conferences if interested.

Key responsibilities:

Work closely with the Principal Investigator in all aspects of the research
Develop data collection systems
Conduct data cleaning and codebook development
Monitor study data and provide biweekly updates to the study team on accumulating data
Prepare analysis datasets and documentation
Facilitate study analysis and assist faculty and post-docs in data analysis activities, including table and figure development for manuscripts
Contribute to quantitative research efforts in the field of HIV epidemiology and prevention
Apply statistical models and use statistical software to derive quantitative research findings
Work as part of a team to develop scientific data from various data sources
Contribute as co-author to manuscripts
Contribute to data visualization output to disseminate study findings

The position will be based at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia. The initial appointment is for 2 years, and renewal is anticipated if performance is satisfactory and funds remain available.

Detailed Project Description:

PREMISE

To reach Ending the Epidemic (ETE) targets, we will need consistent national HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) data to describe patterns of use and to understand which programs and policies are effective at facilitating PrEP uptake. This NIH-funded study aims to build on our history of developing public PrEP data resources and innovative metrics of PrEP use in PREMISE (PrEP Epidemiology, Modeling, and Surveillance), a collaborative and interdisciplinary group that will use national PrEP data, along with legal and policy coding, to inform the US HIV epidemic response. The study will conduct analyses regarding the scope of PrEP scale-up over time and will perform analyses to explore the impact of different locality-specific programs and policies on PrEP use

MISTR+

Our study (MISTR+) seeks to establish an evidence base for telehealth and improve health outcomes in terms of PrEP care initiation, retention, and re-engagement for the over 100,000 users of this service by (1) developing a series of low-touch interventions based on existing evidence and new data analyses of telePrEP electronic records data, (2) testing interventions, and (3) enhancing our understanding of intervention performance through machine learning and cost-effectiveness analysesthat will inform intervention prioritization.

Elección

The HIV epidemic in Latin America is concentrated among MSM. As the number of HIV prevention options grows, it is critical to build interventions that empower individuals to make HIV prevention choices that fit their lives; this requires delineating and addressing barriers, elucidating individual preferences, and providing accessible prevention options. Remote access to health services and information may overcome many challenges of traditional clinic service delivery models. TheElección study will improve our understanding of health determinants for HIV incidence and the prevention and care cascades in Peru. The study will build a cohort to assess HIV incidence and its predictors and to identify intervention preferences. We will adapt and test a digital intervention grounded in participant choice to improve HIV prevention service uptake. Specifically, we will develop an observational HIV incidence cohort (Aim 1), implement discrete choice experiments and use the ADAPT-ITT model to inform adaptation of an evidence-based intervention to the Peruvian setting (Aim 2), and transition cohort members into the clinical trial (Aim 3). Participants will be randomized to either the adapted version of the digital intervention (M-Cubicado) or to observation-only follow-up (standard of care).

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

A bachelor's degree and one year of experience in data analysis, statistics, or a related field, OR an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Master’s degree in Epidemiology, Biostatistics or other relevant quantitative field.
Experience with quantitative data analysis.
Experience using statistical software to derive quantitative research findings.
Excellent scientific writing ability
Experience in data management and analysis using SAS, R or other statistical software.
Experience in analysis of clinical trial and/or national claims data.
Experience in HIV prevention or digital health

NOTE: This role will be granted the opportunity to work from home regularly but must be able to commute to Emory University on a flexible weekly schedule based upon business needs. Schedule is based on agreed upon guidelines of department. This role requires residency in the state of GA. Emory reserves the right to change remote work status with notice to employee.

new_jobs.title: Program Coordinator II, Community Based Research Initiative (Community Engagement & Research Coordin
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary:

Under the general supervision of the Executive Director and Program Principal Investigator, the INSPIRE Programs Coordinator will manage the day-to-day operations of CDU’s growing portfolio of INSPIRE community-based research programs—INSPIRE Faith, INSPIRE CA, and INSPIRE USA. The Coordinator serves as the primary operational point of contact across these programs, combining research-program coordination, community relationship-building, and oversight of the digital engagement and data-capture platforms (in partnership with the technology team) that enable the programs to operate at scale. The role blends hands-on, place-based community partnership (primarily through INSPIRE Faith) with the coordination of predominantly online, largely automated statewide, and national programs. A central purpose of the role is to strengthen community trust in research and to broaden the participation of Black/African American/Hispanic communities and other communities of color in clinical research and trials, ensuring that community voice and priorities shape how the work is designed and carried out.
About the Center:
The Charles R. Drew University of Medicine and Science (CDU), a partner in the UCLA Clinical and Translational Science Institute (CTSI) alongside UCLA and Cedars-Sinai, is building a community-centered clinical research enterprise through its Clinical and Translational Research Center (CTRC) in South Los Angeles. The INSPIRE programs are a family of community-based research initiatives advancing health and brain health across diverse populations. INSPIRE Faith is a deep, place-based partnership with faith institutions requiring regular in-person engagement with community partners; INSPIRE CA, and INSPIRE USA are digitally delivered, largely automated programs conducted primarily online, with select live sessions led by physicians and study staff. Together they build on CDU’s longstanding legacy of community engagement and health-equity research.

This work advances a national commitment to health equity: expanding access to healthcare in underserved communities, building lasting trust between communities of color and the healthcare system, and increasing the participation of Black/African American communities and other communities of color in research and clinical trials. As a historically Black graduate institution, CDU pursues these goals in partnership with peer institutions and community organizations, treating community relationships not as a means of recruitment but as the foundation of research that is shaped by, accountable to, and beneficial for the communities it serves. The INSPIRE Programs Coordinator is central to this mission, serving as the trusted community bridge that connects faith and community partners to research and trial opportunities and helps ensure that the science reflects the priorities of the community.
Essential Duties

Manage the day-to-day operations and coordination of the INSPIRE research programs (Faith, CA, and USA), ensuring each program runs smoothly, on schedule, and in alignment with study protocols and the Center’s mission
Coordinate in-person activities for INSPIRE Faith—anticipated at approximately two days per week of on-site engagement with community partners—and support the logistics of live sessions conducted by physicians and study staff across all programs, including scheduling, participant coordination, and event execution.
Coordinate and support program staff, students, and volunteers across the INSPIRE programs, including onboarding, task coordination, and training
Support participant recruitment, retention, and outreach across programs, including coordinating culturally appropriate promotional and educational materials (in collaboration with the communications team)
Attend community meetings, faith-partner gatherings, health events, and program activities as needed to represent the INSPIRE programs and CDU
Oversee the online engagement platform, participant communications, scheduled calls, and data-capture elements for the digitally delivered programs (INSPIRE CA, and USA), coordinating closely with the technology team to ensure the platforms function reliably and participant data is captured accurately and securely.
Monitor program metrics, participant engagement, and feedback to assess effectiveness, support quality improvement, and inform recommendations to program leadership
Establish and support Faith Community Advisory Boards across Los Angeles, coordinating the formation of one board in 2026 and several additional boards by 2028. Each board is a governance body of no more than 11 faith leaders drawn from partnering faith institutions, guiding program direction, protocol input, and community voice at the faith-partner level. The Coordinator organizes board recruitment, scheduling, meeting logistics, and ongoing stewardship.

Recruit, onboard, and support Community Navigators from partnering faith institutions, growing the Navigator corps to 50 by the end of 2026 and more than 500 by the end of 2028. Navigators are community members who support the conduct of the studies from the faith-community side, including participant recruitment, guidance in navigating different community and clinical spaces, and support at program events. Navigators are distinct from advisory board members and are not study participants themselves.

Organize and help lead faith-based health festivals, coordinating planning, faith-partner engagement, logistics, staffing, and execution to advance community health and program visibility across partnering faith institutions.
Build trusted partnerships with community and faith-based organizations, serving as the primary liaison and fostering ongoing engagement across INSPIRE programs.
Advance community-centered research by connecting partners to clinical research opportunities, promoting diverse participation, and ensuring community voices inform program and study design through transparent and culturally responsive engagement.
Perform administrative tasks related to community engagement program management, such as creating reports, PowerPoint, and maintaining records
Support grant management and reporting for the programs—including tracking deliverables, timelines, and compliance, and coordinating with dedicated grant writers who lead proposal writing (this role is not responsible for writing grants)

Required Qualifications

EDUCATION:

Four-year college degree (B.A., B.S.) in Health Sciences. Experience in Business Administration, Public Administration, or Public Health is an advantage.

EXPERIENCE:

At least 2 or more years of experience coordinating research programs, studies, or educational/community programs, preferably in an academic, clinical research, or healthcare setting and activities.
Experience with grant or program management, including tracking deliverables, timelines, budgets, and reporting requirements for federal, local, or private funders (proposal writing is handled by dedicated grant writers and is not required for this role).

new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

Under the general supervision of the Executive Director and Program Principal Investigator, the INSPIRE Programs Coordinator will manage the day-to-day operations of CDU’s growing portfolio of INSPIRE community-based research programs—INSPIRE Faith, INSPIRE CA, and INSPIRE USA. The Coordinator serves as the primary operational point of contact across these programs, combining research-program coordination, community relationship-building, and oversight of the digital engagement and data-capture platforms (in partnership with the technology team) that enable the programs to operate at scale. The role blends hands-on, place-based community partnership (primarily through INSPIRE Faith) with the coordination of predominantly online, largely automated statewide, and national programs. A central purpose of the role is to strengthen community trust in research and to broaden the participation of Black/African American/Hispanic communities and other communities of color in clinical research and trials, ensuring that community voice and priorities shape how the work is designed and carried out.

About The Center

The Charles R. Drew University of Medicine and Science (CDU), a partner in the UCLA Clinical and Translational Science Institute (CTSI) alongside UCLA and Cedars-Sinai, is building a community-centered clinical research enterprise through its Clinical and Translational Research Center (CTRC) in South Los Angeles. The INSPIRE programs are a family of community-based research initiatives advancing health and brain health across diverse populations. INSPIRE Faith is a deep, place-based partnership with faith institutions requiring regular in-person engagement with community partners; INSPIRE CA, and INSPIRE USA are digitally delivered, largely automated programs conducted primarily online, with select live sessions led by physicians and study staff. Together they build on CDU’s longstanding legacy of community engagement and health-equity research.

This work advances a national commitment to health equity: expanding access to healthcare in underserved communities, building lasting trust between communities of color and the healthcare system, and increasing the participation of Black/African American communities and other communities of color in research and clinical trials. As a historically Black graduate institution, CDU pursues these goals in partnership with peer institutions and community organizations, treating community relationships not as a means of recruitment but as the foundation of research that is shaped by, accountable to, and beneficial for the communities it serves. The INSPIRE Programs Coordinator is central to this mission, serving as the trusted community bridge that connects faith and community partners to research and trial opportunities and helps ensure that the science reflects the priorities of the community.

Essential Duties

Manage the day-to-day operations and coordination of the INSPIRE research programs (Faith, CA, and USA), ensuring each program runs smoothly, on schedule, and in alignment with study protocols and the Center’s mission
Coordinate in-person activities for INSPIRE Faith—anticipated at approximately two days per week of on-site engagement with community partners—and support the logistics of live sessions conducted by physicians and study staff across all programs, including scheduling, participant coordination, and event execution.
Coordinate and support program staff, students, and volunteers across the INSPIRE programs, including onboarding, task coordination, and training
Support participant recruitment, retention, and outreach across programs, including coordinating culturally appropriate promotional and educational materials (in collaboration with the communications team)
Attend community meetings, faith-partner gatherings, health events, and program activities as needed to represent the INSPIRE programs and CDU
Oversee the online engagement platform, participant communications, scheduled calls, and data-capture elements for the digitally delivered programs (INSPIRE CA, and USA), coordinating closely with the technology team to ensure the platforms function reliably and participant data is captured accurately and securely.
Monitor program metrics, participant engagement, and feedback to assess effectiveness, support quality improvement, and inform recommendations to program leadership
Establish and support Faith Community Advisory Boards across Los Angeles, coordinating the formation of one board in 2026 and several additional boards by 2028. Each board is a governance body of no more than 11 faith leaders drawn from partnering faith institutions, guiding program direction, protocol input, and community voice at the faith-partner level.
The Coordinator organizes board recruitment, scheduling, meeting logistics, and ongoing stewardship.

Recruit, onboard, and support Community Navigators from partnering faith institutions, growing the Navigator corps to 50 by the end of 2026 and more than 500 by the end of 2028. Navigators are community members who support the conduct of the studies from the faith-community side, including participant recruitment, guidance in navigating different community and clinical spaces, and support at program events.
Navigators are distinct from advisory board members and are not study participants themselves.

Organize and help lead faith-based health festivals, coordinating planning, faith-partner engagement, logistics, staffing, and execution to advance community health and program visibility across partnering faith institutions.
Build trusted partnerships with community and faith-based organizations, serving as the primary liaison and fostering ongoing engagement across INSPIRE programs.
Advance community-centered research by connecting partners to clinical research opportunities, promoting diverse participation, and ensuring community voices inform program and study design through transparent and culturally responsive engagement.

new_jobs.description:
Back to jobs

New

Behavioral Health Care Manager / Program Manager - Enhanced Care Management

Inland Empire, California

Akido builds AI-powered doctors .
Akido is the first AI-native care provider, combining cutting-edge technology with a nationwide medical network to address America’s physician shortage and make exceptional healthcare universal. Its AI empowers doctors to deliver faster, more accurate, and more compassionate care.

Serving 500K+ patients across California, Rhode Island, and New York, Akido offers primary and specialty care in 26 specialties—from serving unhoused communities in Los Angeles to ride-share drivers in New York.

Founded in 2015 (YC W15), Akido is expanding its risk-bearing care models and scaling ScopeAI, its breakthrough clinical AI platform. Read more about Akido’s $60M Series B. More info at Akidolabs.com.

The Opportunity

At Akido Care, we are redefining healthcare for underserved communities by addressing the needs of populations with complex medical and social challenges. As part of our ECM team in the Inland Empire, you'll be at the forefront of this mission, providing compassionate, impactful care.

We are hiring for two versions of this role, and this posting covers both. Which one fits depends on the experience you bring.

Behavioral Health Care Manager. You will serve as the team's behavioral health resource—contributing to care planning, providing direct patient support, and ensuring that patients in crisis or with unmet behavioral health needs are connected to the right level of care.
Behavioral Health Care Manager & Program Manager. In addition to serving as the team's behavioral health resource, you will supervise an interdisciplinary team of case managers, including but not limited to: a Registered Nurse, Care Coordinator, and Community Health Worker. This version carries a higher salary.

This is a hybrid role based in the Inland Empire, with regular in-person presence at Chaparral Medical clinics (particularly Pomona and Rancho Cucamonga clinics), community outreach in the field, and occasional travel to LA for all-hands meetings. Local candidates strongly preferred.

The minimum education requirement for both versions of this role is an MSW or MFT, with a California licensure (LCSW/LMFT) preferred. You will also need to reside locally to the region served.

What You'll Do — Behavioral Health Care Manager

Maintain a personal caseload of patients with behavioral health needs and deliver high quality care to patients.
Conduct behavioral health screenings and assessments to inform individualized care plans, developed in partnership with the patient and the interdisciplinary team.
Serve as the team's go-to resource for behavioral health questions, warm handoffs, and crisis response protocols—ensuring that patients presenting with suicidality, acute mental health concerns, or SUD crises are appropriately triaged and connected to care.
Document all encounters accurately and timely in Care Director in compliance with IEHP ECM program requirements, CalAIM standards, and HIPAA.
Serve as subject matter expert in team dependent topics such as harm reduction, and clinical case management.
Build, manage, and maintain relationships with key partner organizations.
Contribute to monthly all-hands meetings by sharing success stories and showcasing team impact.

What you'll do — Behavioral Health Care Manager & Program Manager

In Addition To The Responsibilities Above

Team Management and Supervision

Establish a team culture of respect, empathy, and teamwork.
Conduct regular 1:1s to provide feedback, coaching, and support.
Assign new patients to case managers, ensuring balanced and achievable panel sizes.
Ensure your staff meet their required caseload, optimizing care delivery and patient outcomes.
Fully train and onboard new case managers within designated timeframe and ensure they manage a full caseload within designated timeframe.
Build an engaged and resilient team by supporting case managers with burnout prevention and self-care strategies.
Lead recruitment efforts, including resume screening, interviews, and onboarding processes.
Approve timecards, time-off requests, and expense reports for direct reports.

Program Operations

Drive team towards quarterly objectives in collaboration with Director. This includes proactively generating ideas to achieve goals and implementing the agreed upon ideas with direct reports.
Implement quality improvement initiatives to enhance patient outcomes and operational efficiency in collaboration with Director.
Oversee patient care plans to guarantee they are implemented effectively and meet quality standards.
Oversee enrollment and disenrollment of patients in alignment with organizational SOPs.
Collaborate with the Director to meet audit requirements and track team compliance metrics.
Manage budget used for supplies, and other inventory.

Leadership in Akido best practices

Facilitate huddles, weekly data reviews, and care planning meetings.
Represent your team in meetings with the Director and external partners.

Training and Development

Tailor training programs to meet the needs of your team and local environment.
Mentor case managers, focusing on skill-building, professional growth, and patient care excellence. This includes upskilling staff in motivational interviewing, harm reduction, coaching etc.

Who You Are — Behavioral Health Care Manager

Deep understanding of Medi-Cal populations, including those experiencing homelessness, mental illness, or substance use disorders.
Minimum 2 years of experience in behavioral health case management, care coordination, or direct services with Medi-Cal or similarly complex populations.
Exceptional organizational and time-management abilities.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including team coaching and conflict resolution.
Familiarity with compliance standards, documentation systems, and data-driven decision-making.
This person will also need to reside locally to the region served.

Who you are — Behavioral Health Care Manager & Program Manager

In Addition To The Qualifications Above

4+ years experience managing front line staff.
Proven leadership experience, preferably in healthcare or social services.

Preferred Skills And Qualifications

Experience with Medi-Cal/Medicaid populations, CalAIM, or ECM programs.
Familiarity with IEHP and the Inland Empire county behavioral health system.
Experience working with populations experiencing homelessness, justice involvement, or high emergency department utilization.
Bilingual English/Spanish preferred but not required.
Valid driver's license, automobile insurance, and reliable transportation.

License, Certification, And Education Requirements

Master's degree in Social Work (MSW) or Masters in Family Therapy (MFT) required.
California licensure (LCSW/LMFT) preferred but not required; licensed or license-eligible candidates strongly preferred.

Benefits

Health benefits include medical, dental and vision
Paid sick time in accordance in CA law.
Accrued paid time off (PTO)

new_jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Affirm is reinventing credit to make it more honest and friendly, giving consumers the flexibility to buy now and pay later without any hidden fees or compounding interest.

About The Technical Program Management Team

The Technical Program Management team at Affirm operates at the intersection of strategy, product, and engineering execution. We are versatile operators and trusted strategic partners who drive complex initiatives, design our planning engines, and architect operational frameworks that power the technology behind Affirm's business. Guided by our commitment to putting the customer first and pushing the envelope, we elevate how teams collaborate, resolve critical tradeoffs, and turn high-level vision into scalable reality.

About The Role

We're looking for an experienced, motivated Senior Technical Program Manager to oversee high visibility planning programs for our teams and help streamline our processes for building and delivering great customer and merchant products. As our products scale in complexity to meet our accelerating business and expanding product lines, our business and technology process management practices need to scale with it. In this role, you will work closely with engineering, product, analytics, and other cross-functional teams to align efforts with goals, identify opportunities for improvement, and drive change initiatives.

What You’ll Do

Drive complex, multi-disciplinary, and highly visible transformation & operational programs in service of our team’s mission to deliver honest financial products that improve lives
Coordinate and collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders across the company to drive alignment on strategy, priorities, and key decisions.
Implement lean processes and drive towards better ways of working to realize value from planning, ask questions that clarify priorities and push the team to be effective, and build a culture of continuous iteration and improvement
Establish and run data-driven operational frameworks to view portfolio performance against OKRs, accelerate value realization by enabling right investment decisions, influence and train teams on more effective ways of working, and create excitement around change to increase adoption
Develop communication strategies to ensure critical information flows seamlessly across the organization
Partner with cross-functional teams to plan change requirements, identify risks, manage dependencies, and establish tools and forums to drive clarity and efficiency
Identify and distill needs, experiment with new ideas to address systemic inefficiencies and bring transparency, visibility, alignment, and promote accountability across the organization

What We Look For

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience
8 years of proven experience managing programs, processes, and change management in a technology-focused environment
Strong technical background with a deep understanding of software development processes
Organized and strategic approach to collaborating across multi-disciplinary teams
Obsesses over getting the details right but knows how to make tradeoff decisions
Strong stakeholder management with Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, and other cross-functional teams
Track record of successfully implementing frameworks at scale and building relationships in a remote friendly culture
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and consulting skills
Passion and drive to change consumer finance for the better
Prior experience in FinTech, Payments or Commerce is a plus.

Pay Grade - L

Equity Grade - 6

Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include equity rewards, monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents.)

USA base pay range (CA, WA, NY, NJ, CT) per year: $165,000 - $225,000

USA base pay range (all other U.S. states) per year: $146,000 - $206,000

Affirm is proud to be a remote-first company! The majority of our roles are remote and you can work almost anywhere within the country of employment. Affirmers in proximal roles have the flexibility to work remotely, but will occasionally be required to work out of their assigned Affirm office. A limited number of roles remain office-based due to the nature of their job responsibilities.

Benefits

We’re extremely proud to offer competitive benefits that are anchored to our core value of people come first. Some key highlights of our benefits package include:

Health care coverage - Affirm covers all premiums for all levels of coverage for you and your dependents
Flexible Spending Wallets - generous stipends for spending on Technology, Food, various Lifestyle needs, and family forming expenses
Time off - competitive vacation and holiday schedules allowing you to take time off to rest and recharge

new_jobs.title: Case Manager
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Case Manager

Samaritan Daytop Village operates transitional housing programs for single adults and families experiencing homelessness across all five boroughs of New York City. The Case Manager works directly with clients to conduct interviews, evaluate their needs, and collaboratively develop Independent Living Plans. This includes identifying and leveraging community resources, coordinating referrals to services such as healthcare, education, and legal support, and assisting clients in relocating to permanent housing. The role also involves maintaining detailed documentation, monitoring client progress, and advocating on their behalf to help remove barriers to stability and self-sufficiency.

Responsibilities

Build professional relationships with clients and maintain confidentiality
Review client eligibility documents and explore non-shelter alternatives
Create and manage client files and records
Conduct intake interviews and psycho-social assessments
Develop and update Independent Living Plans with short- and long-term goals
Refer clients to permanent housing and community-based services
Support clients in overcoming barriers and advocating for themselves
Track client progress and document updates through regular contact
Follow up with clients and referral agencies to monitor service outcomes
Provide data for required reports (weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual)
Act as a liaison with outside organizations for education, healthcare, childcare, housing, and legal matters

Qualifications

High School Diploma or equivalent required; Associate or Bachelor’s Degree in Human Services, Social Work, or a related field strongly preferred
At least 1 year of experience in case management or social services working with individuals experiencing homelessness, substance use, mental health challenges, or other complex needs
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build trust with individuals from diverse backgrounds
Clear and effective communication skills for conducting interviews, documenting progress, and coordinating with external partners
Ability to maintain accurate records and meet reporting deadlines
Commitment to maintaining client confidentiality and adhering to professional ethics
Familiarity with New York City’s housing, healthcare, legal, childcare, and educational resources
Problem-solving skills and a supportive approach to helping clients overcome challenges
Organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple responsibilities
Culturally sensitive and responsive to the needs of individuals and families experiencing homelessness

Additional Information

The Case Manager role is a full-time non-exempt role with an hourly rate of $25.21 (annualized at 35 hours a week to $45,895) with a full benefits package. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance, 25 days of paid time off, access to a retirement account with an employer to match, and tuition reimbursement.

This role is located in Morris Heights, Bronx and has a schedule of Sunday-Thursday 8am-4pm.

Meaningful, mission-driven work supporting youth and families in real-life settings
Collaborative, team-based care model with strong clinical guidance
Opportunities to grow your clinical skills alongside licensed professionals
Direct involvement in therapeutic interventions and group facilitation
Dynamic, community-based role (homes, schools, courts, and more)

________________________________________

As a key member of the TASK treatment team, you will:

Deliver Community-Based Support

Partner with families, schools, and community stakeholders to implement behavioral supports
Provide crisis response, safety planning, and skill-building interventions
Help youth and families navigate complex emotional and behavioral challenges

Reinforce therapeutic interventions aligned with the TASK model and domains
Assist in clinical processes, including assessments and data collection

Coordinate Care & Advocate for Families

Connect families with critical community resources and support systems
Communicate regularly with court counselors and external partners

Support audits and ensure adherence to program and funder standards

new_jobs.title: Case Manager-Bilingual Spanish
new_jobs.description:
BACKGROUND INFORMATION:

The Center for Community Health (CCH) represents an exciting opportunity for Tulsa. The goal is to improve health disparities in the Tulsa community, decrease re-admission rates and inappropriate emergency room usage, and increase the use of primary care providers to improve Saint Francis Health System (SFHS) patient health outcomes.

POSITION SUMMARY:

Provides services to bridge the gap between Center for Community Health clients and community health services by: Coordinating referrals to community agencies for additional assistance, treatment, and continuity of care. Completes electronic documentation of each client contact. CMs will work closely with medical providers and primary case management teams at SFHS, Laureate, and other agencies to improve client care and outcomes. CMs will primarily work out of SHFS patient rooms and have office space at SFHS and/or Laureate. CMs will implement effective strategies for linking high risk uninsured and underinsured clients to primary care/medical homes; increase access to appropriate health care and community-based services; assist individuals in improving health status; and promote behavior change in using the health care delivery system.
Principal Duties and Responsibilities/Essential Job Functions
The following functions represent most of the duties performed by the position but are not meant to be all-inclusive or prevent other duties from being assigned when necessary.
ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS (95% of Time):

Build trust and rapport with high-risk patients through bedside screening and engagement in hospital, emergency department, and behavioral health inpatient settings.
Provide focused case management by linking enrolled clients to the most appropriate venue for entry into the health care delivery system to include addressing the social determinants of health: transportation, primary care provider, food, utilities, health insurance, medications, housing, domestic violence, and access to internet, phone, and identity.
Coordinate care with SFHS physicians, case management, and other staff to provide coordinated screening for referred patients.Work with a multidisciplinary health care provider team. Participate in weekly meetings and visit identified patients in the hospital before discharge.
Coordinate as needed with Tulsa Health Department (THD) services and community partner resources.
Engage clients through home visits and meet clients in community-based settings such as shelters, hospitals, clinics, and partner agency sites, to deliver outreach, support care coordination, and address social determinants of health.
Participate in and attend regularly scheduled supervision meetings; be prepared to share both successes and pitfalls of case management.
Provide culturally and linguistically appropriate services to assigned clients.
Maintain complete and accurate documentation of all activities and reports through computerized data entry in accordance with program standards, guidelines and THD requirements. This includes preparing and submitting paperwork, such as, Workflow List, Enrollment Questionnaires, Client Summaries, and Weekly Caseload List.
Attend regular peer group meetings for networking and information sharing for optimal care management and navigation.
Other duties as assigned including those required to fulfill activities in support of public health emergency operations.

SECONDARY JOB FUNCTIONS (5% of Time):

Participate in staff meetings, quality assurance activities, and in-service trainings.
Complete monthly time sheet and mileage forms.

Qualifications/Specifications/Knowledge and Skills
Education:
Bachelor’s degree required. Health care, social work, or public health background or education preferred.
Experience:
One-year experience in health care, social work, or public health preferred. Previous experience with low-income individuals and engaging culturally diverse individuals in health and social services is preferred.
Knowledge and Skills:

Bilingual in English/Spanish is required.

Must have ability to work quietly and respectfully in a shared workspace.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills are required to provide effective health counseling and obtain cooperation from individuals who come from a wide range of economic, social, and ethnic backgrounds.
Demonstrated comfort working in hospital and behavioral health settings and interacting with individuals experiencing physical, behavioral, or mental health challenges.
Skill in operating a personal computer and smart phone applications.
Understanding of healthcare delivery processes.
Skills in obtaining and protecting personal health information (PHI).
Effective interpersonal skills in working with personnel at all organizational levels.

Licenses/Certification:

Valid Oklahoma driver’s license required

Supplemental Information
INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL WORKING RELATIONSHIPS:

Regular internal contact with various nurses and case managers to coordinate care or referrals for patients.
External contact with community partners for the coordination of care and referrals for clients.

PHYSICAL EFFORT:

Requires frequent mobility throughout a high-volume hospital environment, including travel between patient rooms, clinical units, and multiple floors.
Ability to visit clients’ homes, conduct interviews, attend meetings, sit for extended periods, and pick up and deliver transportable medical equipment, ie. briefs, shower chairs, wheelchairs, etc.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY/ACCOUNTABILITY:

Direct Supervision – None
Indirect Supervision – None
Budget/Money/Material – Responsible for assigned computer hardware and software
Reports to – Manager, Center for Community Health

Description

FULL DESCRIPTION

If you believe healthcare is a right, that everyone deserves high quality care so they can enjoy their highest level of health and wellbeing, and you value each person's individual story – consider joining us at Neighborhood!

As a community health worker (CHW), you’ll have an important role in creating a positive experience for patients at Neighborhood.

About The Role

You’ll listen with kindness to patients’ concerns, seek solutions, and assist patients and families with navigating services and community resources. Responsibilities include:

Consults with providers regarding patient needs for referrals or linkages and assist patients in accessing and completing referrals.
Assists patients in accessing community resources such as food pantries, clothing, shelter, transportation, education, parenting or other services as referred by providers.
Assist patients in completing healthcare forms such as applications for Medicaid, Child and Family Health Plus and Sliding Fee Scale program. Connect patients to facilitated enrollers.
Obtains prior authorizations as needed. Documents and tracks referrals until completion.
Conducts community outreach to identify people who are experiencing homelessness and educates them about health needs.
Supports people who are experiencing homelessness in accessing healthcare services at Neighborhood.
Serves as health and community resources coordinator for patients and providers.
Advocates for patients with community agencies and services.
Conducts outreach and speaks to community groups.
Assists in developing Neighborhood staff to improve patient navigation, decrease barriers for patients in accessing care and connect patients to care.

You will be primarily based at our Blasdell location, 4233 Lake Avenue, Blasdell.

What It’s Like To Work At Neighborhood

The top three words employees say describe the work environment are: teamwork, supportive, kind
. These are from an anonymous survey of Neighborhood employees for the Buffalo Business First Best Places to Work competition. Neighborhood earned “finalist” distinction in the competition for four consecutive years. We are a group of flexible and kind individuals who are open to each other’s ideas and see opportunities to innovate and find solutions when challenges arise.

Education And Skills

High school diploma
Experience in community health, patient resource coordination or equivalent experience
Medical office and medical terminology knowledge and experience preferred
Attention to detail and follow-through, organizational and influencing skills
Experience with Electronic Health Records (EHRs), Microsoft Office Suite, and other computer software
Excellent oral and written communication skills
Kindness: you treat each person with respect and compassion, valuing each person’s story
Resiliency: you see opportunities to innovate and find solutions when challenges arise
Teamwork: you are open to others’ unique perspectives, and will collaborate to meet shared goals

Must be available to work Monday-Friday between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., and have ability to travel for community outreach and work extended hours once a week 7:00-9:00 p.m.

What We Offer

Compensation: $22.25 an hour based on a full-time, 40-hour workweek

Benefits: You’ll have options for medical, dental, life, and supplemental insurance. We also offer a 403b match, health savings accounts with employer contribution, wellbeing programs, continuing education opportunities, generous paid time off, and holidays.

Services include internal/family medicine, pediatrics, OB-GYN, dentistry, podiatry, psychiatry, vision care, nutrition and behavioral health counseling, and pharmacy services. We’re working toward a Western New York where all enjoy their highest level of health and wellbeing.

Connecting clients, caregivers, families, and Right at Home through trust,

communication, and exceptional care.

It begins with trust.

It begins with relationships.

people are connected at the right time.

That’s where you come in.

We’re looking for a Care Manager
who understands that great home care is about

much more than scheduling caregivers and completing assessments. It’s about creating

a strong connection between our clients, their families, our caregivers, and the Right at

Home team.

The Care Manager is a trusted liaison between the people we serve and the agency

that serves them—someone who can listen to a client’s concerns, recognize

opportunities to improve care, support our caregivers, and make sure important

information doesn’t fall through the cracks.

You’ll be involved from the beginning of the client relationship, conducting initial

assessments and helping families understand how Right at Home can support them.

You’ll stay connected as care evolves, monitor important reports and outcomes, and

help ensure our clients receive the quality, consistency, and responsiveness they

deserve.

You’ll also play an important role in developing and supporting our caregivers—from

conducting new-hire orientations to helping them understand what it means to represent

Right at Home in a client’s home.

If you’re someone who enjoys people, thrives on organization and accountability,

communicates exceptionally well, and takes pride in making things better, we’d love to

meet you.

What You’ll Do

Your responsibilities will include:

 Serve as a primary liaison
between clients, families, caregivers, and the Right

at Home team, ensuring concerns, questions, and important information are

communicated and addressed promptly.

 Conduct initial client assessments
and help develop an understanding of each

client’s needs, preferences, goals, and home environment.

through regular communication, follow-up,

responsiveness, and a genuine commitment to their experience.

and help new caregivers understand Right at

Home’s expectations, culture, policies, procedures, and commitment to quality

care.

 Regularly review RightAssist reports,
identify trends, concerns, opportunities,

and follow-up items, and communicate findings to the appropriate members of

the leadership team.

receive the appropriate guidance, resources, communication, and follow-through.

including onboarding, documentation, employee

Communication, And Other Administrative Responsibilities As Needed.

, helping caregivers feel

connected, informed, and supported while maintaining high standards of care

and professionalism.

 Identify and communicate changes in client needs
, caregiver performance,

scheduling concerns, service issues, or other matters that may impact the quality

of care.

, helping resolve issues before

with clients, families, caregivers,

referral partners, and members of the community.

Who You Are

You’re someone who naturally builds relationships and enjoys helping people.

handle difficult conversations with professionalism and empathy.
